Staff Regulations, 2022
In exercise of the powers conferred upon me under Sections 29 (4) of National Revenue
Authority Act, 2016, I hereby issue the following Regulations:
CHAPTER I
PRELIMINARY PROVISIONS
1. Title and Commencement
These Regulations shall be cited as the “Staff Regulations, 2022” and shall came into force
on the date of its signature by the Minister.
2. Purpose
The purpose of these Regulations is to regulate procedures governing performance and
staff behaviour while on duty
3. Authority and Application
These Regulations are drafted in accordance with the provision of section 29(4) of the Act,
and shall apply to all staffs of National Revenue Authority.
4. Interpretations
In these Regulations unless the context otherwise requires:
“Abusive language” means uttering of any words, drawings, writings, gestures
or otherwise inciting hate, ridicule or contempt towards any
person, gender, sex, group, race, tribe, religion or political
opinion;
“Act” means the National Revenue Authority Act, 2016;
“Appointing Authority” means the Board or the Commissioner General;
“Approved Medical Doctor” means a Medical Practitioner duly registered according to
written laws and engaged by a Medical Institution approved
by the Authority;
“Assets Declaration Form" means a form approved by the Authority for declaring
interests in assets and liabilities established by the Act;
“Authority” means the National Revenue Authority;
“Board” means the Board of Directors established under the Act;
8

“Bribery” means to give, offer, accept or obtain any gift, money or
benefits as an inducement to make or not to make a decision
in favour of the person and for employee’s gain;
“Collective bargaining agreement” means an agreement between employer and trade
union to regulate working salaries, working conditions,
benefits and other aspects of workers’ compensations and
rights for workers;
“Commissioner General” means the Chief Executive Officer of the Authority;
“Criminal Offence” means offence of criminal nature chargeable in a Court;
“Department” means functional unit below division;
“Division” means functional unit in the Authority;
“Demotion” means a reduction of staff grade on disciplinary grounds;
“Disciplinary Authority” means the Board for all staff appointed by the Board and the
Commissioner General for other staff;
“Disciplinary Committee” means the Board or any Committee constituted for the
purpose of investigating, hearing, determining or
recommending on a matter arising from a breach of the Staff
Regulations of the Authority;
“Disciplinary Offence” means any act or omission or misconduct or failure to take
reasonable care or failure to discharge duties in a reasonable
or satisfactory manner by or on the part of staff which
warrants disciplinary proceedings under these Regulations;
“Disciplinary Penalty” means termination, demotion, formal reprimand or a written
warning;
“Domicile” means a place in the Republic of South Sudan where staff
declares to be the permanent home at the time of
employment, provided that a staff may request to change
place of domicile;
“Drug” means any substance that produces physical, mental,
emotional, or behavioural change in the user;
“Staff” means any person who has entered into or works under a
written contract of employment with the Authority;
“Employer” means the National Revenue Authority;
“Family” means spouse, children, father and mother wholly or partly
dependent upon the earning of the staff;
9

“Fraud” means criminally cheating or deliberately attempting to
deceive by giving false information (written or verbal),
including falsifying or attempting to falsify;
“Grievance” means a complaint or dissatisfaction by staff on any
conditions of employment;
“Harassment” means unwelcome verbal or physical behaviour that
interferes with work or creates an intimidating environment,
hostile, offensive work environment, examples include:
public or private bullying by supervisor, subordinate, peer,
severe or repeated insults related to personal or professional
competence; threatening or insulting comments whether oral
of written; deliberate discrimination malicious or knowingly
false complaints against others;
“Insubordination” means deliberate refusal by staff to carry out a lawful
instruction given by a person in authority or any other form
of disobedience or ridicule whether by words or deeds;
“Intern” means a student seconded from a learning institution to
acquire practical work experience in line with their field of
study;
“Job Evaluation” means the process of determining the worth of a job, how
jobs shall be graded on the basis of the education and
training required, the complexity of the work involved and
the responsibility the staff may bear for the results of the
work;
“Long Term Training” means full time training with duration of over six months
leading to an award of a degree, diploma or certificate;
“Management Committee” means a committee composed of managerial staff;
“Managerial staff” means Commissioner General, Deputy Commissioner
General, Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner and
Assistant Commissioner;
“Minister” means the Minister responsible for Finance;
“Promotion” means the appointment of staff to a higher grade;
“Reviewer” means staff occupying a superior position to the immediate
supervisor of the incumbent who reviews the staff
performance;
“Senior Management” means the Commissioner General, Deputy Commissioner
General, Commissioners and Deputy Commissioners;
1 0

“Sexual Harassment” means an act of uses position of authority in exchange for
sexual favour, intimidate another staff or threaten a staff who
refuses to engage in any type of sexual relations or unlawful
act consisting of any physical or verbal behaviour that is
unwelcome;
“Spouse” means a wife or a husband, for the purpose of privileges and
entitlements for which staff qualifies;
“Supervisor” means any person who supervises and appraises a staff under
him or her;
“Suspension” means a temporary removal of staff from exercising the
duties of his or her office after he or she has been convicted
of an offence;
“Termination” means cessation of employment;
“Transfer” means movement of staff from one duty station to another;
CHAPTER II
NATIONAL REVENUE AUTHORITY ORGANISATION STRUCTURE AND
OBLIGATIONS
5. Organisation Structure
(1) The Board shall approve the Organization Structure of the Authority based on
the optimum requirements; the Commissioner General shall forward the same to
the Minister who shall table it to the Council of Ministers for final approval.
(2) The Commissioners shall determine their staffing needs in consultation with the
Commissioner for Corporate Service, there shall be no increase in the establishment
at any grade or at any station, without the approval of the Commissioner General.
(3) Staff may be re-deployed between departments including stations for positions,
which do not involve promotions at the discretion of the Commissioners in
consultation with the Commissioner for Corporate Service.
6. Authority Divisions
The Authority is structured into five divisions and three independent departments which
report directly to the Commissioner General.
7. Domestic Tax Revenue Division
(1) The Domestic Tax Revenue Division is charged with the administration of non-
oil tax revenue.
1 1

(2) The Division shall be headed by a Commissioner who shall be responsible for
the day to day running of the division subject to the direction of the Commissioner
General and Board on matters of strategic policy.
8. Customs Revenue Division
(1) The Division is responsible for facilitation of trade and for collection of import
duty, import sales tax, export duty, import excise and other taxes in accordance with
Customs Act.
(2) The Division is to ensure the protection of revenue by preventing smuggling, this
shall be done by physically patrolling the borders and other strategic points,
examination of goods, and search of premises, as well as documents relating to the
goods.
(3) As a frontline institution at the country's borders, Customs Division also plays a
key role in surmounting external aggression and maintains the territorial integrity.
(4) The Division shall be headed by a Commissioner who shall responsible for the day
to day running of the division subject to the direction of the Commissioner General
and the Board on matters of strategic policy.
9. Corporate Service Division
(1) The Corporate Service Division covers the management of Finance, Human
Resources, Administration, ICT Research and Planning Departments of the
Authority.
(2) The Division shall be headed by a Commissioner who shall be responsible for
the day to day running of the division subject to the direction of the Commissioner
General and Board on matters of strategic policy.
10. Internal Audit Division
(1) The Internal Audit Division shall be responsible for conducting internal audit to
ensure that the Authority’s rules and procedures are adhered to and internal controls
are operating as prescribed in the internal Audit Manual, Financial Regulations and
applicable Public Financial Management and Accountability Act.
(2) The division shall be headed by a Commissioner who shall be responsible for the
day to day running of the division subject to the direction of the Commissioner
General and the Board on matters of strategic policy.
11. Internal Affairs Division
(1) The Internal Affairs Division shall be responsible for assessing Authority’s ethical
and integrity climate and drive strategies, regulations and policies to achieve the
desired level of staff compliance to legal and ethical requirements.
1 2

(2) The division is also responsible for conducting both reactive and proactive special
investigations on the allegations levelled against staff members.
(3) The Division shall be headed by a Commissioner who report to the Commissioner
General and the Board on matters of strategic policy.
12. Taxpayer Service and Education Department
(1) The Taxpayer Service and Education is responsible for the authority’s external
communications as well as taxpayer service, information and education.
(2) The department is headed by a Deputy Commissioner who reports directly to the
Deputy Commissioner General.
(3) Staff under the taxpayer service and education are vested with responsibility of
registration of taxpayers at the divisional level under the Assistant Commissioner
reporting administratively to the Commissioner of Domestic Tax Division and
functionally to the Deputy Commissioner for Taxpayer Service and Education.
13. Legal Service and Board Affairs Department
(1) The department provides legal interpretation and support to Authority operations
on legal and board matters.
(2) The division shall be headed by a Deputy Commissioner who shall be responsible
for the day to day running of the department subject to the direction of the
Commissioner General and the Board on matters of strategic policy.
14. Procurement and Logistics Department
(1) The Department provide technical expertise and oversee the effective management
of the procurement of goods, works and services to ensure timely availability and
standards desired.
(2) The department is headed by a Deputy Commissioner who is responsible for day to
day running of the department and report to the Commissioner General and Deputy
Commissioner General.
15. Management Committee Meetings
There shall be monthly Management Committee Meetings to discuss policy, strategies
and operational issues of the Authority.
1 3

16. Integrity Committee
(1) There shall be Integrity Committees at Authority Headquarters, Revenue
Divisions, State Revenue Offices and Customs.
(2) The main functions of these Committees shall be to devise and oversee the
Observant of the C o d e o f C o n d u c t.
(3) The Commissioner General shall appoint members of Integrity Committees and
provide specific terms of reference for every Integrity Committee.
(4) The Commissioner General shall report to the Board on quarterly basis, the
progress on the o b s e r v a n c e o f t h e C o d e o f C o n d u c t and give the status of
integrity and ethics climate in the Authority.
17. General Obligations
(1) The Authority operations are based on confidentiality, trust and honesty.
(2) All staff are required to represent great loyalty, unquestionable integrity and
willingness to protect the interests of the Authority.
(3) The following serve as basic guides to staff in preventing commission of any act
which shall reflect adversely upon the staff or the Authority:
(a) every staff shall conduct himself or herself private affairs in a manner not
intended to discredit or disrepute the Authority;
(b) every staff shall at all times both inside and outside the Authority premises,
whether on duty or not, behave in a manner as befit any employee of the
Authority, in particular, the staff shall exercise discreetness and common sense
in their dealings with members of the public;
(c) every staff shall perform his or her official duties in accordance with the
general instructions laid down by the Authority.
CHAPTER III
RECRUITMENT AND APPOINTMENT OF STAFF
18. Recruitment Policy
(1) The Authority recognizes that the preferred recruitment method is through an open
and competitive process, applications shall be considered when a specific position,
or a pool of positions, is being staffed, when voluntary applications are submitted,
the Human Resource Department shall keep database of the applications for
consideration alongside other applications through advertisement in accordance
with the Act.
1 4

(2) Authority shall employ competent citizens of the Republic of South Sudan
whenever possible; non- citizens may be employed only when it is not possible to
find a competent citizen with suitable qualifications and shall be on contract on a
specified term.
(3) The Authority is committed to recruit high calibre staff for successful attainment of
its objectives.
(4) The Authority is an equal opportunity employer, it shall provide equal access to
employment and ensure that the best available person is appointed to any given
position free from discrimination on the basis of race, gender, religion, ethnicity,
language, political, nationality, disability, pregnancy or HIV status.
(5) The Authority may engage temporary staff from time to time in order to
supplement staff requirements, staff hired under this status shall be remunerated
in accordance to the terms stipulated in the contract, temporary employment
contract shall be for a maximum period of ninety (90) days.
(6) The Authority is committed to develop and promote its staff, any vacancies which
may arise for positions other than Board appointees, shall be filled by a suitable
staff through interdepartmental transfers or internal advertisements. In the
absence of a competent internal candidate, vacancies shall be filled by competitive
recruitment.
(7) The Commissioner for Corporate Service in liaison with the relevant Division or
Department shall handle the recruitment process.
(8) The Management or the Board may appoint an external recruitment agent or
institution to assist in the recruitment process, provided that the final approval
shall remain a responsibility of the respective Appointing Authority.
(9) Appointments, promotions, or transfers to any post in the Authority shall adhere to
qualifications as may from time to time be specified as necessary for appointment
to the post.
(10) The Authority shall:
(a) embrace an open and competitive approach to recruitment and recruit the
qualified candidates for jobs as advertised based on merit. The recruitment and
selection process shall ensure the identification of the person best suited to the
job and the Authority;
(b) encourage the recruitment of staff with disabilities and shall make reasonable
adjustments to all stages of the recruitment process and as required in order for
a successful candidate with a disability to undertake the post;
(c) ensure that in the recruitment process at least thirty-five percent (35%) gender
rule is implemented according to the laws of the Republic of South Sudan;
(d) ensure that employment represents the face of South Sudan, that employment
shall transcend tribal and religious affiliations;
1 5

(e) ensure that the recruitment and selection of staff is conducted in a
professional, timely and responsive manner and in compliance with current
employment legislation;
(f) provide appropriate training, development and support to those involved in
recruitment and selection activities in order to meet the objectives of the
Authority;
(g) Authority shall treat all applicants fairly, equitably and efficiently, with respect
and courtesy, aiming to ensure that the candidate experience is positive,
irrespective of the outcome;
(h) ensure that its recruitment and selection process is cost effective;
(i) ensure that if a member of staff involved in the recruitment process has a close
personal or familial relationship with an applicant, he or she shall declare this
as soon as he or she is aware of the individual’s application and avoid any
involvement in the recruitment and selection decision- making process;
(j) ensure that all documentation relating to applicants are treated confidentially;
and
(k) ensure the information provided by an individual seeking employment is
authentic.
19. Recruitment and Selection Procedures
(1) The Authority staff recruitment shall take into account the need for new ideas,
approaches and commitment to ensure national diversity in her workforce.
(2) Vacancies in the approved staff establishment shall not be filled without a duly
authorized Staff Requisition Form together with a job descriptions and performance
indicators, these forms shall be filled by the Head of Department requesting
additional staff and submitted to the Commissioner for Corporate Service, the
respective heads of department shall be expected to provide the following:
(a) a justification for the new position;
(b) detailed job description and specifications;
(c) proposed entry level; and
(d) job specifications shall be updated for any vacant position(s) and approved by
the Board.
(3) The job specifications shall state mandatory criteria in terms of skills, aptitudes,
knowledge and experience for the job, all of which shall be directly related to the
job and applied equally to all applicants and to ensure that criteria used do not
indirectly discriminate against certain groups of applicants.
(4) New positions shall get the approval of the Commissioner General, where such
positions are for senior management positions, approval shall be sought from the
Board, the Commissioner of Corporate Services shall cause the approved vacant
positions to be filled as appropriate.
(5) As a minimum requirement, all positions shall be advertised within the Authority
for permanent employment, in the event that the internal advertisement has not
attracted the suitable candidate, the Authority shall advertise vacant positions in at
1 6

least one (1) national daily newspaper with wide circulation, and also on the
Authority’s website, the advert shall remain open for a period of at least fourteen
(14) days.
(6) Application letters for all positions shall be addressed to the Commissioner
General and that short listing of candidates shall be done under the supervision of
the Commissioner for Corporate Service. All shortlisted candidates shall be invited
for an interview.
(7) There shall be interview panels to conduct interviews, the interview panels shall
comprise a minimum of three (3) panellists selected by the Commissioner General
based on the level of recruitment. Where recruitment is at senior level, a Board
member shall form part of the panel, the Authority shall hire an expert to assist in
the absence of in-house expertise.
(8) All candidates shall be assessed objectively against the selection criteria set out in
the job requirements as advertised and according to other relevant provisions of the
law.
(9) Minutes and final report of interview duly signed by the panellists shall be in the
custody of the Commissioner for Corporate Service.
(10) All interviewed candidates shall be notified of the outcome within two (2) weeks
from the day of the interview.
(11) In special cases, the Authority may head-hunt a staff, this shall apply to senior
positions and head-hunting shall be approved by the Board where the target staff has
special and rare skills necessary for the advancement of the Authority, such staff
may be sought from outside South Sudan.
20. References
(1) A candidate shall be required to provide the names and contact addresses of
persons who may be prepared to voluntarily give frank, honest and objective
attestation of the candidate's qualifications, work, and conduct among others. The
information shall be treated with utmost confidentiality by the appointing authority.
The referees provided by the candidate shall include:
(a) persons from academic institutions attended;
(b) previous place of employment; and
(c) persons who have deep knowledge of the candidate's background.
(2) The employer reserves the right to verify any academic or professional certificate
submitted in support of the application for employment.
(3) At least two referees shall form part of the documentation requirements for all job
applicants.
1 7

(4) If the appointment is urgent, the Commissioner for Corporate Service may seek to
obtain a verbal or telephone reference for the successful candidate provided that
standard procedures for doing so are followed and approved by the Commissioner
General.
(5) Referees shall be contacted with or without the candidate’s consent and the
information provided shall be treated as confidential by the panel members.
21. Background Check and Verification of Certificates
(1) The Commissioner for Corporate Service shall be responsible for background
check and verification of certificates from the relevant institutions for all
successful candidates.
(3) All staff to be appointed to the positions of Chief or Principal Officer and
above shall be vetted, at the discretion of the Commissioner General.

23. Medical Examinations
All new staff shall undergo a medical examination at the cost of the Authority with an
appointed medical facility. The appointment shall be subject to a candidate being
declared medically fit by an approved Medical Doctor, who shall communicate the results
confidentially to Authority through a duly filled form.
24. Staff Bio data
All newly appointed staff shall fill in staff bio data form on reporting for duty and shall
notify the Human Resources Department in writing of any change of name, address, and
other relevant personal particulars within thirty (30) days of any change, the
particulars shall be updated regularly in the personal file and in the system as and when
the change is notified.
25. Staff Declaration Form
(1) All staff have a duty not to disclose without proper authority any information that
has been obtained in the course of official duties, this includes all documents,
records, and information stored electronically.
(2) Engagement in any of the following ways shall be considered as misuse of
official information and may lead to disciplinary action:
(a) leaking information;
(b) use of information for personal or private gain;
1 9

(c) taking advantage of a person on the basis of information gained through
official records; and
(d) removing, altering or destroying official records.
(3) All staff shall complete declaration form and submit to the Head of Department
responsible for Human Resources.
26. Staff Identity Cards
(1) The staff shall be issued with identification cards indicating their particulars as
they are assigned to access the premises during working hours.
(2) The Heads of Department or Division shall determine staff to be issued with staff
identification card when on duty outside Authority premises and shall be required
to produce their identity cards on demand.
(3) Staff whose identity card requires replacement shall produce an authentic proof
of loss or damage before replacement from right authority (police and Human
Resource Department).
27. Staff Probation Period
(1) Staff appointed on permanent or contractual terms shall serve a probationary
period of three (3) months.
(2) The respective Head of Department shall carry out a performance appraisal to
determine suitability for confirmation for permanent employment or termination as
the case may be, such appraisal shall be carried out and communicated to the
Commissioner for Corporate Service at least one month before expiry of the
probation period, the concerned staff shall be notified of the performance appraisal
results in writing.
(3) In case of an interruption during the course of probation, the probation may be
extended to cover the period of absence.
(4) The probationary period may be extended for a period not exceeding three months
if management deems it necessary, where the staff probationary period is extended
the staff shall be informed in writing.
(5) The Appointing Authority or a newly appointed staff on probation may
terminate appointment at any point before the probationary period expires by
giving a twenty-four (24) hours’ notice.
28. Confirmation of Appointment
(1) Confirmation shall take effect from the date when the staff completes
satisfactorily his or her probation, where the probation is extended, confirmation
shall take effect from the date when the staff completes the extended probation.
2 0

(2) The Commissioner for Corporate Service shall issue a letter of confirmation soon
after the approval of the respective Appointing Authority.
29. Letters of Appointment
(1) When approval for an appointment has been granted, a letter of appointment
shall be issued, setting out the main terms and conditions of service, salary
offered and details of the position.
(2) The offer of appointment shall include as far as possible the job description
and performance standards for the job, the candidate shall immediately confirm
acceptance of an offer and indicate the date of reporting for duty, the offer of
appointment shall be valid for six weeks from the date of offer.
(3) Letters of appointment and Contracts for employment shall be in writing, signed
by the Commissioner General or any other officer authorized to sign on his or her
behalf and by the staff on the other part. Employment shall be on contractual or
permanent and pensionable terms and this shall be specified in the contract.
(4) Acceptance of an offer for a new appointment by a staff shall be construed
as denouncement of the previous post and respective terms and conditions of
employment.
(5) Staff may be appointed on temporary or casual basis upon identification and vetting
by Human Resource Department, without requirement of external advertising and
structured interviews.
(6) All successful candidates shall be appointed and report within three (3) weeks
from the date of appointment unless a written extension period has been approved
by the Commissioner General.
(7) The appointed candidate(s) shall notify the Commissioner General the
acceptance of offer by returning an appointment letter duly signed within fourteen
(14) days from the date of appointment.
30. Reporting Procedures
(1) New staff shall report to the Human Resources Department at the beginning of
their first day of employment where they shall complete the necessary paperwork
as an ‘employment package’ which shall be used to initiate their payroll formalities,
appropriate employee benefits and to set up their personal file.
(2) Information on pay and mode of payment and the necessary facilities available
shall be given to the staff, the new staff is required to complete or provide the
following information and documents:
(a) a letter of employment and terms and conditions of service duly signed;
(b) copies of the current Curriculum Vitae (CV) and relevant certificates;
(c) two color passport-size photographs of the employee and his defendants;
(d) personal records form;
2 1

(e) originals and copies of relevant statutory documents such as National Identity
Card, driving license, passport; and
(f) a staff bank details.
31. Recruitment of a Retired Person
A person who has reached compulsory retirement age may be re-appointed to the services
of the Authority after obtaining the approval of the ministry responsible for public
service following recommendation by the Board.
32. Appointment of Convicted Person or Persons with known Criminal Records
(1) A person who was previously convicted of a criminal offence or who has been
previously removed or dismissed from the public service shall not be appointed
to the service of the Authority.
(2) Where it is found that a staff has been appointed in contravention of these
Regulations, the appropriate Appointing Authority shall nullify such
appointment immediately.
33. Declaration of Assets and Financial Interest Form
Without prejudice to section 28 of the Act, there shall be declaration of assets and
financial interest form:
st
(a) the form shall be submitted at the end of each calendar year on or before 31
December;
(b) the staff is required to declare all assets and liabilities:
(i) in his or her possession or ownership;
(ii) in the possession or ownership of his or her spouse;

CHAPTER IV
INDUCTION, ORIENTATION, TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT
34. Induction
(1) All new staff shall undergo an induction program so as to facilitate their easy
settlement in the new appointment and for quick familiarization with the Authority,
the Human Resources department in liaison with the respective Departments shall
ensure all new staff are inducted.
(2) The Recruitment Section in the Human Resources shall maintain an induction
guidelines booklet and shall develop a comprehensive induction program for the
new staff.
(3) The Human Resources Department and the receiving Division or Department shall
provide the new staff with the necessary information to enable them blend in.
2 2

35. Orientation
(1) It is the policy of the Authority to conduct orientation programs for new staff
as a process of disseminating information and providing direction.
(2) Orientation introduces staff to their new environment by providing them with the
tools and knowledge they shall need to understand and adapt to their new
workplace in order to work productively.
(3) New staff shall be introduced to the Authority and particular departments,
locations, colleagues, rules and regulations, reporting times, break, lunch and
leaving time shall be conducted by the Human Resources and Administration
Departments in conjunction with the concerned Heads of Department.
(4) The staff shall be given an opportunity to seek clarification on what may not be
clear to him or her about their new job, the Human Resources and Administration
Departments shall provide the staff with the orientation guidelines booklet,
orientation periods may vary from a minimum of three (3) days to a maximum of
ten (10) days.
36. Transfers
(1) Transfer is a movement of a staff from one of the services within the Authority to
another or from one class of posts to another class of posts within the same or
different service, this may involve a change of designation and duties, the
Commissioner General or designated officer shall approve the transfer of a staff
where the exigencies of the service require the transfer to be made.
(2) The Authority may transfer a staff either on temporary terms or on long term at
any time as may be deemed necessary, temporary transfers shall not extend beyond
ninety (90) days after which the staff shall either be permanently transferred or
returned to his or her original station.
(3) A staff may request to be transferred to new stations, such staff shall submit his
or her application to the Commissioner for Corporate Service through Head of
Department, with the exception of staff requesting for transfer on medical grounds
all other staff applying or requesting for transfer shall be required to meet the cost
for such transfers and shall not be entitled to transfer allowance.
(4) The Commissioner for Corporate Service shall maintain registry of staff
transfers.
(5) If any vacancy arises at any station, the Commissioner for Corporate Service shall
first go through the Transfer Application Register to determine whether there are
any recorded applicants for the position at the requested workstation. If no request
exists for transfer it may be the discretion of the Commissioner for Corporate to
nominate candidates for transfer through the Commissioner General.
2 3

37. Training and Development
(1) Training and development is the key to ensure that the staff are equipped to meet
present and future needs and challenges, the acquisition of skills, knowledge and
the development of managerial and leadership know-how is critical for the effective
management of the staff, it is the foundation of responsiveness, accountability and
innovation.
(2) The overall aim of training in the Authority is to deliver cost effective training
to all staff, to provide technical knowledge and personal skills to be able to
perform their duties effectively and develop in their careers.
(3) There shall be an approved annual training plan and budget prepared by
Commissioner for Corporate Service and approved by the training committee.
(4) Authority shall endeavour to secure sponsorship for its training plan, staff shall be
encouraged to go for training on self-sponsorship provided that training is in the
approved training plan, the approved training plan shall be circulated to all staff for
information.
(5) Training for the purposes of this Regulations includes, inter alia, training courses,
programs, seminars, workshops, individual lessons, and on the job training or
coaching under the guidance of a trainer or facilitator to improve the performance
of individual staff of the Authority.
(6) Training shall always take place in South Sudan; this does not exclude the
Authority from engaging training providers from outside the Country.
(7) Staff shall seek approval through their respective supervisors to the Head of
Human Resource Department to confirm the budget and the skills and knowledge
gaps before recommending to the Commissioner General for ultimate approval to
train in an approved skill gap identified in the staff appraisal.
(8) Participation of a staff in long term training requires the staff to sign a prescribed
bonding form with the Authority setting forth the terms and conditions of such
participation.
38. Eligibility for Training
(1) Participation in training shall be subject to training needs assessment conducted by
the Commissioner for Corporate Service, each staff shall be required to undertake
at least one training per year in order to improve competences and skills.
(2) Interns, visiting or sabbatical professionals and consultants are not eligible for
training activities.
(3) The following criteria shall be used in selecting staff for long training:
(a) the staff shall be admitted by a recognized institute;
2 4

(b) the staff shall be confirmed and has worked with the Authority for a
minimum of one year after confirmation or previous training;
(c) good performance and integrity;
(d) equal opportunity and gender sensitive; and
(e) a course shall be relevant to the business of the Authority.
(4) Staff on contract term appointment may be eligible for short external training, if
their appointment does not expire within six months after the day of completion of
the training.
39. Training Needs
(1) There shall be regular training needs analysis exercises to determine the
priority training requirements, performance appraisal reports, future staffing
requirements, departmental strategic objectives and the corporate plan shall provide
information.
(2) The responsibility for the identification of training needs shall be vested in the
line managers in collaboration with the Commissioners, Department and Section in
the Authority and individuals may also identify their need for training.
(3) The Authority shall utilize interactive processes when identifying priority training
needs, managers, supervisors and staff shall work together to identify priority
training needs and agree on the competences that may be needed to ensure both the
business and individual success.
(4) The process of training needs assessment shall be done annually and projection for
training made, the Head of Division or Department responsible for Human
Resource shall coordinate the training needs assessment.
40. Professional Qualifications
Authority shall sponsor its staff in terms of study program, tuition and examination fees to
pursue professional qualifications in line with the approved training plan
41. Attendance to Training
(1) Staff shall be released to attend training approved in the training plan after
receiving confirmation of admission.
(2) A staff who declines without any reason a training nomination applicable
to his or her position shall be subjected to disciplinary action.
42. Annual Training Plan and Budget
(1) All training provided by the Authority shall be based on identified training needs
of either the employee or the Authority as determined through performance
2 5

appraisal reports, training needs assessment, future staffing requirements and future
work programmes.
(2) Commissioners or Department shall prepare departmental annual training plans
and forward them to the Head of Division responsible for Human Resources for
compiling.
(3) The training plan shall, include the following:
(a) title of the course;
(b) target group;
(c) number of staff;
(d) course provider;
(e) venue of the course;
(f) duration and cost involved; and
(g) source of funding, objective of the course and justification for the course.
43. Funding for Training
(1) The Authority may provide the lead in funding staff training and development by
setting aside a certain percentage of the annual budget.
(2) The Authority shall facilitate training under special arrangement through the
following ways:
(a) scholarship from external sponsors;
(b) scholarships from special projects;
(d) cost sharing sponsorship by the Authority and external donors; or
(e) private or self-sponsorship by the staff and reimbursable scholarship.
(2) Each scholarship shall be awarded according to selection criteria as stipulated in
these Regulations.
(3) staff who qualifies for any of the sponsorship provided in these Regulations shall
only proceed on study leave after approval has been granted.
44. Sponsorship
The Authority may support training needs in the following ways:
(a) leave with pay;
(b) leave with pay and all attendant expenses paid for by the Authority;
(c) leave with pay and partial expenses paid by the Authority;
(d) leave without pay and staff to pay all their expenses; or
(e) time-off during regular work-time.
45. External Scholarships
(1) The Authority shall solicit for scholarships from the government and various donor
organizations for sponsorship of staff for training.
(2) Sources of external scholarship are:
2 6

(a) external Governments or agencies;
(b) international organizations; or
(c) international financial institutions.
46. Sponsorship for Long Term Training
(1) Sponsorship to long term training shall include both undergraduate and
postgraduate studies.
(2) Staff requesting release to pursue relevant long-term full-time training
under private sponsorship where such course is not in the training plan may be
granted leave without pay for the duration of the course.
(3) Staff on approved long-term training fully sponsored by the Authority or any other
sponsor shall be paid full salary.
(4) For the purpose of creating a favorable learning environment for staff attending
local full-time long-term training under the Authority sponsorship, direct training
cost payable to student may be determined by the Management from time to time
47. Salary Adjustment and Re-categorization
(1) Staff salary may be adjusted, if the qualifications attained are in accordance with
the scheme of service, the adjustment shall be with effect from the date the
employer receives the respective certificate.
(2) Staff acquiring relevant qualifications shall be promoted/re-categorized in
accordance with scheme of service, re-categorization shall be with effect from
the date the employer receives the respective certificate.
48. Progress Report
Staff attending long term training shall be required to submit progress reports, for staff
fees for the following term or semester shall not be paid, if the report is not submitted
unless there is a justifiable reason.
49. Performance Appraisal During Training
Training shall be regarded as part of work, training progress reports from the
respective institutions shall be incorporated in the annual performance appraisal.
50. Repeating a Year
Staff on training shall be allowed to repeat a year only once and at own cost during the
tenure of the course unless it is proved that it was on medical grounds.
2 7

51. Discontinuation from Studies
(1) Staff discontinued from training or who failed to acquire the desired qualification
from long term training for academic reasons shall not be sponsored or released
by the Authority to pursue long term training.
(2) Discontinuation from studies on disciplinary grounds shall be regarded as a
gross misconduct warranting formal disciplinary proceedings.
52. Re-sitting Examinations
The Authority shall not incur any expenses related to the re-sitting of examinations
except for professional examinations where the Authority may meet the cost only once
per each part of the examination.
53. Training Committee
(1) There shall be a Training Committee, which shall make decisions on the
utilization of training resources within the Authority subject to approval by the
Commissioner General.
(2) The Training Committee shall be composed of the Deputy Commissioner General
as Chairperson, Commissioners, Head of Departments, or any member co-opted by
the Committee from time to time, the Assistant Commissioner for Human
Resources shall be the Secretary of the Committee, the Committee shall meet at
least once in every quarter.
(3) Divisions or Departments shall have a Divisional or Departmental Training
Committee that shall consider all applications for training and recommend them to
the Authority training committee.
54. Training Bond
(1) Any staff who is granted study leave by the Authority for a period longer than
six (6) months shall be required to serve the Authority for a period equal to the
study leave.
(2) Any staff who is paid stipend by the Authority for a period longer than six (6)
months shall be required to serve the Authority for a period equal to the period paid
for stipend.
(3) Where a staff is paid stipend for a period of three (3) years or more, he or she shall
be bonded for three (3) years after completion of the course.
(4) Staff who are granted study leave with pay for a period longer than six (6) months
shall sign a bond at the beginning of the study leave.
2 8

(5) In cases where bonds overlap, they shall run concurrently, if one leaves the
Authority employment before, he or she completes the bond period, the recipient
employer shall normally be required to pay for both bonds.
(6) Staff who train privately on programs with prior approval of the management may
be reimbursed and shall be bonded at the time of reimbursement, the bonding period
shall be calculated on the basis of the duration of the normal training programs.
(7) Staff who breaches the bond shall be required to reimburse the full or part of
the costs as may be specified by the management.
55. Payment of Salary and Emoluments to Staff on Training
When a staff attends to a full-time training for a period longer than six (6) months on an
external sponsorship or Authority sponsorship, such a staff may be granted leave with
salary for the specific period of the program as per the prevailing public regulations.
56. Staff Succession Plan
(1) Succession plan is a vital strategic Human Resource Management tool that shall
not be ignored by the Authority, it deals with projecting future changes by
anticipating vacancies and then determining how to meet these challenges.
(2) Succession plan is a systematic process where managers identify, assess and
develop their personnel to ensure that they are ready and capable of assuming key
roles within the Authority, having this process in place is vital to the success of the
Authority because the staff who is identified in the plan will eventually be responsible
for ensuring that the Authority is able to tackle future challenges effectively.
(3) The high potential personnel shall be selected carefully and provided training and
development including mentoring and coaching to give them the skills and the core
competencies needed for the authority’s future environment and goals.
(4) Succession plan creates an effective process for recognizing, developing and
retaining top leadership talent that is ready to assume leadership roles in the
authority when the need arises.
(5) Succession plan and development for the future leaders need to reflect the
Authority’s strategic goals, the following key issues shall be considered when
implementing an effective succession plan:
(a) the support and backing of the authority's senior level management staff shall be
obtained;
(b) the plan shall be part of the integrated Human Resource process that
includes training, development and performance appraisal
(c) identifying the skills needed by the authority in the short, medium and long term;
2 9

(d) identifying critical positions for inclusion in the authority's succession planning
programme;
(e) Identifying high-performers that are almost ready to step into the critical
positions;
(f) analysing the workforce and identifying personnel who may be eligible for
retirement within the next five (5) years;
(g) identifying the responsibilities, skills and competencies that will be needed by the
replacements that shall be made;
(h) establishing a system for communicating succession planning information to
heads of division, departments and units;
(i) establishing a systematic approach for identifying, nominating and selecting
potential successors
(j) reviewing background information on successors such as their education,
experience, skills, appraisals and prospects;
(k) determining the training and development requirements of potential successors;
(l) developing the skills of potential successors through work experiences, job
rotation, projects and other challenging assignments;
(m) establishing a system for monitoring the progress of the personnel's development
plan by senior management;
(n) establishing a system of feedback and encouragement to potential successors; and
(o) ensuring that the succession plan belongs to the organization and not the
Human Resource Department or Unit so as to ensure that the plan receives the
attention that it deserves.
CHAPTER V
DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES
57. Disciplinary Measure
(1) Disciplinary Procedures under these Regulations are in accordance with applicable
existing Labour and Civil Service laws.
(2) The primary aim of disciplinary measure is to regulate staff behaviour in order to
ensure that they conduct themselves in an acceptable manner and ensure a fair and
consistent approach to enforce standards of performance.
(3) Staff shall undergo counselling and verbal warnings as first step towards
disciplinary action for misconducts which are considered not being serious
offences under these Regulations.
(4) Disciplinary procedures under these Regulations are designed to cover minor offences
(Summary proceedings) and major offences (Formal Proceedings) to Correct behaviour
and encourage improvement.
3 0

58. Minor Offences
(1) Minor offences are minor acts that a staff is alleged to have committed, which are
not of such gravity to warrant termination in the event of him or her being found
guilty as specified in schedule 1 of these Regulations.
(2) If the supervisor finds that the staff is guilty of an offence and that the offence
falls under minor offences shall:
(a) counsel the staff or issue a verbal warning; or
(b) if the conduct of the staff has not improved following counselling or verbal
warning or if the misconduct requires stronger action than a verbal warning the
supervisor shall:
(i) inform the staff in writing the reason for the action, and give the staff an
opportunity to make representations, during this process, the staff may opt
to have a representative;
(ii) after having considered any representation made, the supervisor will decide
whether or not to give the staff a written warning, any warning shall be
issued to the staff in accordance with a prescribed form and a copy to the
Commissioner for Corporate Services;
(c) where the staff is aggrieved by a written warning, he or she may complete the
prescribed form within five (5) working days after receipt of the decision and
hand it to the next level of the management for decision.
(d) the next level of management considering the appeal shall consider the written
representations contained on the prescribed form and may speak to the person
concerned to obtain additional information but no formal hearing shall take
place.
(e) the authority considering the appeal shall inform the staff on the outcome of the
appeal within five (5) working days from the day of receipt of the appeal.
59. Preliminary Investigation
(1) There shall be form a Investigation Committee to establish the facts.
(2) Before any disciplinary action is taken, the Authority shall carry out a preliminary
investigation to establish the facts relating to misconduct and whether or not the
disciplinary action shall be taken against alleged staff.
(3) Major Offences are the disciplinary offences which, if committed by staff may
warrant his or her termination as specified in schedule 2 of these Regulations.
(4) Formal proceedings for a disciplinary offence shall be instituted against a staff after
he or she has been served with a charge or charges stating the nature of the offence
which he or she is alleged to have committed.
3 1

(5) The charge or charges shall be prepared by the Head of Division responsible
for Human Resource after receipt of the report on the preliminary investigation as
may be deemed necessary.
(6) A disciplinary charge or charges shall be in the prescribed Notice Form and shall
state briefly the nature of the offence which the accused staff is alleged to have
committed together with statement of the allegations on which each charge is based
in the language that the staff may reasonably understand.
(7) A charge or charges shall be accompanied by notice which shall be in the
prescribed Notice Form and shall be addressed to the accused staff inviting him or
her to state in writing, within such period as may be specified in the notice, the
grounds upon which he or she relies to exculpate himself or herself.
(8) Formal charge instituted under these Regulations shall not be invalid by reasons of
any irregularity in the charge or charges save that, such irregularity may be
corrected. Where the charges served against staff are defective, the disciplinary
authority shall be allowed to substitute them with the proper charges at any time
before the date of hearing, provided that the defect so alleged is curable.
(9) Where a staff has been served with a charge and fails to make a representation in
writing giving the ground upon which he or she relies to exculpate him or herself
within the period specified in the notice accompanying the charge or charges, or
make representations which in the opinion of the disciplinary authority does not
amount to a complete defence of the offence of which the accused staff is charged
the Disciplinary Authority shall appoint three or more members, to hold an inquiry
into the charge or charges.
(10) Where the Disciplinary Authority is satisfied that the representations made by the
accused staff amounts to a complete admission of the charge or charges against
him or her, it shall not be necessary to hold any further inquiry or investigations in
respect of such charge or charges, the inquiry committee shall proceed to record the
findings of guilty.
(11) Where the Disciplinary Committee is of the opinion that it may be desirable for it
to be assisted in the conduct of the inquiry by person(s) who may be more
conversant with any professional or technical matter likely to arise in the course
of proceedings, may request the disciplinary authority to assign other person(s)
with the necessary qualifications or experience to assist the committee.
(12) Where a staff or a representative absconds to attend the hearing or frustrate or delays
hearing, the Disciplinary Committee may determine the case ex parte.
60. Formation of Disciplinary Committee
(1) There shall be constituted a Disciplinary Committee to handle disciplinary cases.
3 2

(2) The Minister shall constitute a disciplinary committee for senior management level and
the Commission General for the rest.
61. Inquiry Procedures
(1) The Disciplinary Committee shall adhere to the following procedures:
(a) staff shall be informed in writing of the time, date and place of hearing, the
notice shall be given not less than five (5) days before hearing date;
(b) staff shall be informed of the right to choose another staff to represent him or
her at the hearing to provide assistance, the staff providing assistance may be a
trade union representative;
(c) The staff and the representative or representatives are entitled to be present at
all times during the hearing and shall be informed of the facts of the case against
the staff, an interpreter may be provided by the employer, if required;
(d) before any hearing, the Chairperson of the Disciplinary Committee shall ask the
staff as to whether there is any member in the meeting whom he or she thinks
his or her presence may occasion miscarriage of justice on his or her part, in
such circumstance the staff shall justify, how the presence of the member may
lead to failure of justice on his or her part, the Chairperson shall make decision
on such preliminary objection raised by the staff.
(e) if the staff objects to the presence of the Chairperson, the Disciplinary Authority
shall be informed and requested to appoint another person to Chair the
proceedings.
(f) a management representative shall present the case in support of the allegations
against the staff and the staff shall be given an opportunity to respond to the
allegations, at the hearing parties shall have the right to call witnesses and
question any witnesses called by the other party.
(g) the committee conducting the inquiry shall record the gist of the evidence
adduced before it.
(h) after hearing of the evidence, the Disciplinary Committee shall make a decision
based on a balance of probabilities as to whether the staff is guilty of the
allegations or not, if the Committee is undecided, the staff shall be given a
benefit of doubt.
(i) the decision of the Disciplinary Committee shall be made by way of vote of
majority and in case of equal votes the Chairperson shall have a casting vote.
(j) the question of guiltiness and the penalty to be imposed may be considered
separately and the staff or the representative is entitled to make representations
with regard to an appropriate penalty to be imposed, mitigating and aggravating
factors to be considered shall include the:
(i) seriousness of the offence and the likelihood of repetition.
(ii) staff’s circumstances (including personal circumstances, length of service
and previous disciplinary record).
(iii) nature of the staff’s job (including health and safety considerations).
(iv) circumstances of the infringement itself.
(k) subject to the provision of these Regulations, a committee conducting an
inquiry may regulate the procedure at the inquiry in the manner it may think fit
without occasioning miscarriage of justice on either part;
3 3

(l) the inquiry shall be concluded within a period of sixty days from its
commencement;
(m) the Authority shall bear the cost if the staff invites his or her fellow to represent
him or her in disciplinary case;
(n) the staff shall not be victimized for any evidence adduced in favour of his or
her fellow staff.
(2) Upon conclusion of the hearing, the committee shall forward the record of the
proceedings together with its report on the hearing to the disciplinary authority for
a decision.
(3) Upon receipt of the Disciplinary Committee report, the Disciplinary Authority
shall decide on the appropriate decision:
(a) the Disciplinary Authority will inform the staff of the outcome of his or her
decision within a period of thirty days, giving brief reasons for a decision
through Commissioner for Corporate Service;
(b) staff may have the right to appeal against any disciplinary action, within fifteen
(15) days from the receipt of the decision to the board for board appointees and
to Employee Justice Chamber for the rest of the staff.
62. Qualifications of a Member of the Disciplinary Committee
A member of the Disciplinary Committee shall be:
(a) senior grade and above;
(b) grade higher than the grade held by the accused staff;
(c) having no interest of any nature to the dispute;
(d) provided that one of the members shall have sufficient knowledge, skills and
competency in practice in the area related to the allegation.
63. Interdiction from Duty
(1) Staff may be interdicted from duty pending the outcome of the investigations
and the decision of the disciplinary authority, the reasons for interdiction include,
but not limited to the following:
(a) the staff’s presence at work may obstruct the investigation; or
(b) the staff’s on-going performance of duties may present a problem whilst the
investigation takes place.
(2) The authority to interdict shall lie with the Commissioner General, Deputy
Commissioner General and Commissioners for their respective staff.
64. Suspension from Duty on Criminal Proceedings
(1) Staff charged with criminal offence may be suspended on full remuneration pending
a final determination by a court and any appeal there to on that charge.
3 4

(2) Where a staff has been convicted of a criminal offence the disciplinary authority may
suspend that staff from performing his or her duties and functions pending
consideration of the case on disciplinary ground under the provisions of these
Regulations.
(3) Staff on interdiction or suspension shall be entitled to salary, housing allowance
and medical assistance, the staff shall be required to report to the designated office
once a week and may need prior written permission before travelling out of the duty
station.
(4) If no disciplinary proceeding has been commenced in respect of disciplinary
offence, but proceedings for criminal offence are instituted against the staff in any
court of law, disciplinary proceedings shall not be commenced until after the
conclusion of the criminal proceeding.
(5) If disciplinary proceeding has been commenced and during the pendency of such
proceeding, criminal proceedings for the criminal offence arising from the same
facts are instituted, the disciplinary proceeding shall be held and no further step
shall be taken in respect of that disciplinary proceedings until after the conclusion
of the criminal proceedings.
(6) Where disciplinary proceedings have been commenced and concluded against the
accused staff and the staff is acquitted of the criminal charge on a legal technicality,
the acquittal shall not be a bar to disciplinary proceedings against the accused staff
on the same facts, disciplinary proceedings may be instituted against the staff and
may be punished for disciplinary offence as if no criminal proceeding had been
instituted against him or her.

CHAPTER VI
WORK ATTENDANCE
66. Hours of Work
(1) The official working week of the Authority consists of five (5) working days from
Monday to Friday. Commissioners are responsible for ensuring that the regular
hours of working are adhered to.
(2) The official working hours for all staffs at the Authority is from 08:00 A.M. to 5:00
P.M. from Monday to Friday excluding Public Holidays, with a one (1) hour lunch
break from 1:00 P.M. to 2:00 P.M. in such circumstances the lunch breaks shall
be spread to allow continuous coverage and services to internal and external
customers.
67. Variation of working hours
(1) Individual working hours may vary according to the job function but not falling
below eight (8) hours per working day.
(2) Where a specific task demands, staff shall be called upon to work additional hours
or over the weekends. In such cases, overtime payment or off duty shall be made
as stipulated in the Authority terms of Service.
(3) Staff shall arrange to take some compensatory time off in lieu of extra time
worked, this time off shall be recommended to the Commissioner General through
the Head of Division responsible for Human Resources in writing as forwarded by
the section head and shall only be granted at the convenience of the Authority.
(4) Approved time off shall be forwarded to the Commissioner for Corporate Service.
(5) Staff who work in busy offices and are paid extraneous allowances (as stipulated
in this Regulations) shall be required from time to time to work longer hours as
need arises, all staff shall observe punctuality at all times.
68. Attendance
(1) A record of attendance shall be maintained in every work station of the Authority.
(2) It is the responsibility of every staff to be at his or her place of work by the
scheduled starting time.
3 6

69. Staff shall be required to remain and work continuously at their work places during the
prescribed working hours unless permitted by the supervisors.
70. In the event that staff is not able to be at his or her place of work on time, he or she shall
notify the respective supervisor in good time, perpetual tendency of lateness without valid
reasons shall result in disciplinary action.
71. Staff may be absent from work as a result of illness, injury or personal genuine reasons
and approved as leave taken, in such cases, staffs are expected to give their supervisors
sufficient notice before the scheduled starting time, this notification is necessary to
facilitate proper arrangements for work in the absence of the staff.
72. When there is need for a staff to be absent from work, he or she shall request in writing
by filling application for short leave form and obtain approval in advance from the
immediate supervisor.
73. Excessive absenteeism where staff constantly fails to report to work without permission or
excessive lateness adversely affects productivity and over-burdens other staff, who shall
cover for the absentee, these are grounds for disciplinary action, up to and including
dismissal.
CHAPTER VII
LEAVE
74. Annual Leave
(1) Leave is a vital human resource management mechanism that ensures the
promotion of a healthy and productive workforce life and organizational
development.
(2) Annual leave shall be taken within the leave cycle for the purpose of this regulation
“leave cycle” is a period of one year calculated from the date of appointment,
provided that a newly appointed staff shall be required to complete a minimum of
eight (8) months before being granted annual leave.
(3) An employee is entitled to annual leave with full pay as follows:
a. After continuous service of one year or more but less than three years,
twenty-one working days per year;
b. After continuous service of three years or more but less than fifteen
years, twenty-five working days per year; and
c. After continuous service of fifteen years or more, thirty working days
per year
(4) Annual leave for a newly appointed staff working less than six months after
employment shall be calculated on pro-rata basis.
3 7

(5) Annual leave entitlement applies to all staff other than casual and temporary
staffs whose leave entitlement is as stipulated in their contract agreement the staff
become eligible for leave after completion of probation period (three months) with
the Authority.
(6) staff may take his or her annual leave at such time or times as agreed with his
or her supervisor, provided that the Authority shall not unreasonably refuse staff
request for annual leave.
(7) Leave periods shall be scheduled in advance and shall be approved by the staff’s
Head of Department at the beginning of every year.
(8) Staff are encouraged to take all their annual leave due within the stipulated leave
cycle. Leave not taken within the leave cycle shall accumulate from year to year,
once leave is accumulated, it shall be taken at a convenient time as approved by the
Head of Division or Department.
(9) Where a staff has accumulated two years of untaken annual leave, he or she may,
by written agreement, with the Authority, accept financial compensation for half
of the untaken annual leave entitlement.
(10) The Authority shall pay a staff for any annual leave not taken by or paid out to the
staff at the termination of employment, irrespective of the cause of such
termination or to the Administrator of the Estate in the event of staff death.
(11) The Authority shall not require or permit staff to work for the Authority during
any period of leave, provided that the Authority reserves the right to recall staff
from leave, if this is deemed necessary.
(12) In the event a staff is recalled from leave, the recalled staff shall take the
remaining portion of the leave in the subsequent leave cycle or at a date
convenient to both parties, travel expenses will be refunded to the staff upon
submission of documentary evidence.
(13) Staff proceeding on annual leave may, when he or she avails at least one-half of his
or her annual leave, be paid his or her salary in advance for the month in which the
staff proceeds on leave three days before departure from his or her station of work,
this arrangement does not constitute an advance of salary.
75. Application for Annual Leave
(1) Request for leave shall be made on the prescribed leave application form, seven (7)
days prior to the date requested and signed by the staff’s supervisor.
(2) The form shall be sent to the Department of Human Resources for verification of
actual entitlement against the number of days requested.
(3) staff shall not proceed on leave without the prior approval of the relevant authority.
3 8

71. Sick Leave
(1) If it is realized that the staff may be unable to work due to illness or injury, the
Authority shall grant sick leave, the staff shall notify his or her supervisor of the
need to take sick leave, and anticipated duration of such sick leave, as soon as the
staff becomes aware of his or her incapacity to work.
(2) The Authority may require the staff to provide a medical certificate from a
government hospital or private clinic, verifying the staff incapacity arising from
illness or injury and the anticipated duration of staff incapacity to work.
(3) Staff is entitled to a maximum of up to twelve (12) sick-off days on full pay per
year of continuous service, sick leave is not cumulative and shall not be carried
over to the next year.
(4) Unsupported sick leave shall be recovered from the staff’s leave entitlement or
salary.
(5) The Management may refuse to grant sick leave if the sickness is self-inflicted
or due to gross negligence on the staff’s part.
(6) In the case of sick leave and or convalescent leave rendered necessary by the
staff own neglect or misconduct, his or her salary may not be paid to him or her for
the whole period of absence from duty.
72. Illness while on Leave
(1) In the event of illness occurring while staff is on annual leave or any other form of
leave, the period of absence shall continue to be regarded as the original leave for
the full period of the illness, but if the illness extends beyond the expiry of leave
being taken, sick leave shall be granted, if necessary, from the end of such leave
period.
73. Unpaid Leave of Absence
(1) Staff is entitled, on request, to a period of unpaid leave for such reasons as:
a. observing or attending to religious or cultural ceremonies or practices;
b. caring for a family member who is suffering from a serious illness or injury
and who depends on the staff for essential care;
c. undertaking study relevant to the work performed by the staff for Authority;
and;
d. accompanying staff’s spouse, in circumstances where the staff’s spouse is
required to move outside South Sudan for work.
(2) Unpaid leave requested by staff under these Regulations shall:
a. not be unreasonably refused by the management;
3 9

b. be subject to such terms and conditions as are agreed in writing between
the Authority and the staff.
(3) All applications for such unpaid leave shall be sent to the Commissioner for
Corporate Service with recommendations from the Head of Division or
Department.
(4) All such applications shall confirm that all leave due to the staff has been utilized,
unpaid leave of absence shall be subject to approval by the Commissioner General.
74. Maternity Leave
(1) A female staff shall be entitled to a full paid maternity leave of ninety (90) days
and at least six (6) months from the date of return from maternity leave for
breastfeeding while working for half day as stipulated in sub-section 7 below.
(2) The m a t e r n it y leave is inclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and Public Holidays.
For the purpose of this Section, a medical certificate may be issued by an approved
medical doctor or a midwife, the maternity leave shall be exclusive of annual
leave for the year in which the maternity leave is taken
(2) A female staff wishing to extend maternity leave for purposes of caring for her
child, may be granted leave without pay for a period not exceeding one (1) year.
(3) Staff who intends to take maternity leave in accordance with these Regulations
shall give at least fourteen (14) days’ notice of her intention to proceed on maternity
leave, the application for maternity leave shall be supported by a medical certificate
indicating the date on which maternity leave shall commence.
(4) A period of maternity leave taken before the anticipated date of childbirth shall be
extended by the time, if any, between the anticipated and actual date of childbirth,
and the period of compulsory maternity leave following childbirth shall not be
reduced on that account
(4) The m a t e r n it y leave is inclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and Public Holidays.
For the purpose of this Section, a medical certificate may be issued by an approved
medical doctor or a midwife, the maternity leave shall be exclusive of annual
leave for the year in which the maternity leave is taken.
(5) A staff, who has a miscarriage or a stillborn child, shall be entitled to leave for six
(6) weeks after miscarriage or stillbirth.
(6) Where staff requires more time before or after childbirth over and above the
stipulated entitlement, she may apply for annual or unpaid leave up to a maximum
of one (1) month. A female staff shall not forfeit her annual leave on account of
taking maternity leave.
4 0

(7) Staff who returns to work after maternity leave and is nursing her child shall be
entitled to a period of at least six months from the date of her return to the following:
(a) two breaks of thirty (30) minutes each during working day;
(b) a reduction of sixty (60) minutes from her daily hours of work; or
(c) provision of a clean space for baby-seaters in workplace for lactating
mothers to breastfeed their babies regularly.
(8) The entitlement to nursing breaks provided by subsection 319 of Labor Act 7 above
is in addition to any other rest periods to which an employee may be entitled; and
shall be considered as working time with pay accordingly.
(9) Staff shall not work within six (6) weeks of the birth of her child, unless a
medical practitioner certifies that she is fit to do so.
(10) The Authority shall not require or permit a staff who is pregnant or nursing a child
to perform work that is hazardous to her health or the health of a child.
(11) Following a period of maternity leave taken in accordance with these Regulations,
a staff shall have the right to return to the position that she held immediately before
the maternity leave.
(12) Within the premises, of the Authority may plan to have nursing home for
breastfeeding mothers.
75. Paternity Leave
(1) A male staff shall be granted paternity leave with full salary pay for a maximum of
two (2) weeks within a year provided that the staff submits a proof that his wife has
delivered, the paternity leave shall be taken:
(a) within three (3) days after birth of his or her child or
(b) immediately following miscarriage by his wife.
(2) Staff with more than one spouse shall only be entitled to a maximum of two (2)
weeks paternity leave annually.
(3) A male staff with more than one (1) spouse, he shall be entitled to paternity leave
only in respect of the wife registered in the employment records and such leave
shall be taken not more than once in a year.
76. Study Leave
(1) The Authority shall grant study leave to staff pursuing additional academic or
professional qualifications.
4 1

(2) Study leaves not exceeding three (3) years may be granted to staff who has
completed at least two (2) years in service with the Authority provided that
he or she produces documentary evidence from authentic sponsor and that the
programme is in the training plan.
(3) The study leave request shall be submitted to the Commissioner for Corporate
Service through the Head of Division or Department and shall be approved by the
Commissioner General upon being satisfied with the application.
(4) The approval and duration of the study leave shall be dependent on the relevance
of the course to the Authority resource availability and duration of the course in
accordance with sub-regulation (2) of this regulation.
(5) Staff on fixed term contract and those under probation shall not be entitled to
long term study leave.
(6) The Authority shall follow the laid down procedure for processing study leave
requests by staff bearing in mind the needs of the Authority and shall pay the staff
on study leave 100% of their basic salary.
76. Staff on study leave shall not be entitled to annual leave or allowances applicable to day-to-
day work.
77. A staff whose request for study leave has not been approved may opt to apply for unpaid
leave of absence to pursue his or her course, the study leave shall be limited to the duration
of the course.
77. Compassionate Leave
(1) On compassionate grounds such as serious illness, injury or death of an immediate
member of the family (father, mother, sibling, spouse and children), compassionate
leave may be granted for up to fourteen (14) days full pay in a year.
(2) The affected staff shall apply for compassionate leave to the Commissioner for
Corporate Service through his or her supervisor.
(3) Untaken compassionate leave entitlement shall not accumulate from year to year.
78. Leave for Vocational and Union Training or Function
(1) The Authority shall grant leave of absence with full pay to staff who is a member
of a workers Union to attend training, workshop, seminar or function sponsored by
the union internal or external bodies.
(2) The Union shall furnish the management with a list of its officials who are to attend
such training or function in appropriate time.
4 2

79. Public Holidays
(1) The Authority shall observe all official public holidays as recognized by the
Government.
(2) Staff is entitled to paid leave on such days as are declared by the Government to be
public holidays.
(2) If paid holiday falls within an employee’s leave period, the holiday shall not be
counted as a leave day.
(4) Staff who is required to work on a public holiday shall be entitled to:
(a) two (2) times that staff regular hourly rate for all time worked on the public
holiday; or
(b) one day paid leave by way of compensation.
80. Sabbatical leave
(1) In order to broaden the experience of staff and increase their potential value to the
Authority, staff may be granted sabbatical leave, provided that staff on fixed
term contract shall not be entitled to sabbatical leave.
(2) The sabbatical leave may be granted after five (5) years of continuous service
with the Authority.
(3) Sabbatical leave may be granted for a minimum of six (6) months and maximum
of one (1) year with full pay, provided that the Authority shall not meet the
travel expenses and subsistence allowance related to sabbatical leave.
(4) staff on sabbatical leave shall continue to enjoy medical benefits while in South
Sudan.
(5) staff who has been granted sabbatical leave shall not be considered for another
sabbatical leave until the expiry of five (5) years.
(6) The sabbatical leave may be approved at the discretion of the Commissioner
General.
81. Leave Compensation on Termination of Contract
staff who has not availed himself or herself for the annual leave due for the year in
which his or her employment ceases shall be entitled to payment of cash in lieu of annual
leave at the end of his or her contract.
82. Special Leave
4 3

The Commissioner General may at his or her discretion grant special leave for any purpose
not covered by the categories of leave set out in this Regulations, in granting such leave,
the Commissioner General shall take into account the frequency of such absences by the
staff and the effect on a staff work.
CHAPTER VIII
ATTACHMENT AND INTERSHIP
83. Attachment or Internship
(1) For the purposes of mentoring, coaching and imparting skills, attachment and
internship shall be allowed for short periods of 3 three (3) months.
(2) Interns shall not work in sensitive areas of the Authority.
(3) The Authority has provided a clear framework that guides and gives direction, on
the management of all internship or attachment programs and training within the
Authority as follows:
(a) the internship programme shall be implemented after approval by the
Commissioner General.
(b) Commissioners or Department shall identify strategic areas in which the
internship can be implemented
(c) all interns shall upon being accepted as interns be made aware of their rights
and obligation
(d) all supervisors shall mentor interns throughout their learning period.
(4) Internship or Attachment may attract some monetary emolument to support the
intern to travel to and from the station he or she is attached to, the amount of which
shall be determined by Commissioner General from time to time.
84. Acceptance of Interns
(1) Applications for attachment or internship shall be submitted to the Commissioner
for Corporate Service.
(2) Once the Authority receives applications or requests for attachments, the
departments shall be required to declare the number of interns they can take up at
any given time.
85. Terms of Internship Service
(1) The period of internship shall not exceed three (3) months in any one year from the
time of entry.
(2) All persons performing internship shall be expected to have accident insurance
cover at their own cost.
(3) Interns shall be expected to adhere to the rules and regulations, set out in these
Regulations.
4 4

86. Attendance to in-house Training Programs
During their period of engagement, interns may attend any Authority in-house trainings
provided for all staff members.
87. Monitoring and Evaluation
(1) Interns shall be attached to a mentor who shall monitor their performance and
provide the necessary assistance for better learning.
(2) On completion of the internship period, a performance evaluation by the head of
unit is to be conducted to provide constructive feedback from both parties.
(3) The intern shall prepare an end of internship report which shall be discussed with
the relevant Head of Department during an exit interview.
88. Period and Termination
(1) Internship shall commence on the day the intern starts and last for three (3) months.
