(2) During the three months of internship, either party hereto may terminate this
agreement by giving one-week written notice to this effect.
CHAPTER IX
STAFF MEDICAL SCHEME
96. Medical Insurance Cover
(1) The Authority is committed to the promotion and maintenance of the physical and
mental health of its staff and the provision of adequate risk cover for the staff and the
work environment. In pursuance of this objective, the Authority shall ensure that every
staff works under satisfactory, safe and healthy conditions.
(2) The Authority shall provide all eligible staffs with a medical insurance cover as per
the Authority terms of service.
97. Eligibility
(1) The Authority medical insurance cover shall apply to all staff and shall also cover:
(a) one (1) legal spouse;
(b) children of staff (including legally adopted children) who are dependent on the
staff support, and are (18) years old and below, shall be included in the Medical
Scheme;
(c) children in the above category who are eighteen (18) years but below twenty-
five (25) years, undergoing an approved full-time course of higher learning or
other approved education shall be included in the medical scheme with the
approval of the board; and
4 5

(d) any other children of staff may be accepted in the scheme on payment of
capitation fee on a monthly basis at the discretion of the Management.
(2) Medical Scheme shall cover staff, one wife and not more than six (6) children.
(3) In exceptional circumstances, the Commissioner General may extend the maximum
age, subject to the Board’s approval
98. Ineligible Persons
The Medical Benefits Scheme shall not cover and no benefits shall be paid to:
(a) the divorced spouse of staff;
(b) staff who is on casual or temporary terms, his or her spouse or dependents;
(c) staff or his or her dependents where the illness to eligible person is caused by his or
her own neglect, misconduct, intoxication, impropriety or where the illness is as a
result of dangerous sports.
99. Services under the Medical Scheme
The Scheme shall provide medical attention in respect of various services which are
indicated in the terms and conditions of the medical scheme.
100. Medical Transport Expenses
The Authority shall meet the expenses of transport in connection with medical attention and
hospital treatment as approved in the medical scheme.
101. Medical and Hospital Treatment Abroad
(1) A staff or an eligible member of his or her family shall not be considered for medical
treatment abroad except on recommendation of an approved medical practitioner,
Medical Commission and approved by the Commissioner General.
(2) The Authority to incur expenditure for medical treatment outside South Sudan shall
be subject to approval by the Board.
(3) Where staff who is outside South Sudan either on Authority business or for the
Authority-sponsored course falls ill and receives medical attention or treatment
outside South Sudan, the Authority shall reimburse such costs as provided for in
the medical scheme upon production of original receipts from a licensed medical
practitioner in that country.
102. In - patient Expenses
The Authority Medical Scheme shall cover the following In-patient expenses:
(a) Consultation fees and evacuation costs directly leading to hospitalization;
(b) Hospital admission costs;
4 6

(c) ICU/HDU charges, physiotherapy, radiotherapy and chemotherapy;
(d) Theatre charges, costs of surgical appliances and toiletries;
(e) Road and air ambulance for emergency evacuations;
(f) Specialist Doctors’ fees;
(g) Medical investigations and pathology such as X-rays, scans, assorted laboratory
tests;
(h) In-patient ophthalmological (eye), ear, dental treatment and management arising
out of sickness or injuries.
(i) Prescribed medications, dressings and costs of surgical appliances and toiletries.
(j) Day-care surgeries and procedures subject to pre-authorization;
(k) Treatment for pre-existing cases, chronic conditions and HIV/AIDS
management plus related conditions, the chronic ailments include diabetes,
hypertension, asthma, renal failure, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis,
spondylitis, liver diseases, eczema among others.
(l) Congenital conditions covered within the pre-existing or chronic conditions.
(m) Psycho-effective illnesses e.g. mania or depression;
(n) Laser surgery treatment and cataract surgery;
(o) Family planning and infertility treatment.
103. Excluded Medical Cases
The following cases are excluded in the medical scheme:
(a) General or routine health check-ups.
(b) Intentional self-injury, chronic drunkenness, drug and substance abuse.
(c) Cosmetic surgery and beauty treatment unless necessitated by accidental injuries.
(d) Treatment other than by registered medical practitioners.
(e) Amount (rebate) recoverable from health insurance schemes.
(f) Treatment by chiropractors, Acupuncturist and Herbalists.
(g) Injuries as a result of active participation in riots and strikes.
104. Insurance Cover Limits
If the Authority outsources medical scheme services for its staff, the in-patient and out-
patient limits shall be as prescribed from time to time in such Medical Scheme.
105. Funeral Assistance
(1) Upon death of a staff excluding temporary or daily paid staff, the Authority shall
provide burial assistance to cover:
(a) body preparation expenses;
(b) coffin, shroud, grave digging;
(c) transportation of the body to the place of burial;
4 7

(d) transportation of a surviving spouse and children to and from the place of burial;
and
(e) Condolence at the amount to be determined by management.
(2) Upon death of staff, spouse or child the Authority shall provide burial assistance
specified f o r the staff and condolence at the amount to be determined by the
Management.
105. Occupational Health and Safety
(1) Authority shall ensure safe and healthy working environment for staff and visitors
to the Authority premises, the Authority shall provide and maintain the following:
(a) control the health and safety risks arising from work activities.
(b) a safe place of work with safe means of entry and exit.
(c) a safe plant, equipment and systems of work.
(d) necessary information, instruction, training and supervision to protect safety and
health at work.
(2) Authority shall have a regular health and safety consultation with staff and their
representatives and, where necessary with contractors and suppliers of safety
equipment and services, to ensure that occupational health and safety management
is of the highest standard.
(3) The Authority shall strive to avail a comprehensive range of programs to staff to
support their health, safety and wellbeing and the return to work of ill or injured
staff, including ensuring training and instruction is provided to staff commensurate
with their roles and responsibilities to enable them to comply with these
Regulations.
106. Reporting Unsafe Conditions or Practices
(1) Staffs are expected to continually be on the lookout for unsafe working practices,
when a staff observes an unsafe condition, he or she shall warn others, and report
that condition to his or her supervisor immediately.
(2) If a staff has a question regarding the safety of his or her workplace and
practices, he or she shall ask his or her supervisor for clarification.
(3) When staff observes a colleague with an unsafe practice, he or she is expected to
mention this to the colleague and report to his or her supervisor, safety at work
shall be a team effort.
107. Using Safety Equipment
4 8

(1) The Authority shall provide its staffs with appropriate safety equipment and
devises at the workplace.
(2) Staff are required to use the equipment or device provided in the manner designated
as proper and safe by the manufacturer, failure to properly use safety equipment
may lead to disciplinary action, up to and including termination.
(3) If a staff requires safety equipment that has not been provided, he or she shall
contact his or her supervisor before performing the job for which he or she needs
the safety equipment.
108. Reporting an Accident or Injury
(1) Staff are required to report an injury, accident or safety hazard immediately to their
supervisor, who shall in turn report to the Commissioner for Corporate Service.
(2) The Human Resource department shall report an accident or injury to the
insurance company within twenty-four (24) hours of the occurrence of the accident
to ensure that insurance and statutory concerns are adequately complied and dealt
with.
(3) Serious injuries shall be reported on the prescribed injury or accident report form
available in the office of the Department of Human Resources and Administration.
(4) In the case of an accident that results in injury, regardless of the degree of injury,
staff shall notify their supervisor, failure to report an injury could affect a
subsequent workman's injury benefits claim.
109. Smoking at the Workplace
(1) The Authority shall provide a smoke-free environment for its staff and customers
smoking of any kind is prohibited inside the office and within work areas unless in
a designated area.
(2) Supervisors shall inform all those working under them of this smoke-free policy and
take necessary action or report to higher authority any violation of this Regulations.
(3) The Authority shall designate a smoking zone.
110. Violence and Weapons
(1) The Authority believes in open, friendly and supportive working environment for
all staff, violence or threats are prohibited.
4 9

(2) Staff are strictly prohibited from bringing any weapons, including knives, power
saws, axes, and guns or any other offensive weapons or objects to the work areas
or office.
(3) Neither threats of violence nor fighting shall be tolerated, staff are expected to
immediately report to their supervisor any violation of these Regulations.
(4) Any staff found threatening another staff, fighting and or carrying weapons to the
office shall be subjected to disciplinary action.
111. Substance Abuse
(1) the Authority shall provide a safe and productive workplace for its staffs. In
keeping with this commitment, rules regarding alcohol and drug abuse shall be
established for all staff.
(2) The following rules shall apply to all staff during working hours, while they
are on the Authority premises or elsewhere on the Authority’s business are
prohibited from:
(a) The manufacture, distribution, possession, purchase or sale of controlled
substances of abuse on the Authority premises.
(b) Being under the influence of illegal drugs, alcohol or substances of abuse on
the Authority premises.
112. HIV / AIDS
(1) Government shall ensure the necessary policies for managing HIV/AIDS in the
work place are developed and implemented, this shall include:
(a) counselling services;
(b) maintenance of confidentiality about civil servants who are infected or affected
by HIV/AIDS.
(c) provision of care and support;
(d) special care and support for pregnant mothers infected with HIV/AIDs; and
(e) provision of ARV treatment.
(2) The Authority shall maintain a safe and healthy work environment for all staffs
including those with HIV infection and AIDS.
(3) Staff living with or affected by HIV infection and AIDS shall be treated with
compassion and understanding.
(4) Recognizing the need for all staff to be accurately informed about HIV infection
and AIDS, the Authority shall make information and educational materials and
seminars on HIV/AIDS available, staff who wish to obtain information and materials
shall contact the Human Resource Unit or their respective Departmental Head.
5 0

(5) All staff are expected to cultivate good working relationships with any staff who
has HIV infection or AIDS, staff who refuse to work with, withhold services from,
harass or otherwise discriminate against with HIV infection or AIDS shall be
subject to disciplinary procedures.
(6) Information about staff medical condition is private and shall be treated in a
confidential manner. In most cases, only managers directly involved in providing
reasonable accommodation or arranging benefits may need to know staff’s
diagnosis. Others, who may acquire such information, even if obtained personally
from the individual, shall respect the confidentiality of the medical information.
(7) The Authority shall deal humanely and appropriately with staff who are HIV
positive or with AIDS by establishing a supportive workplace environment.
113. Fire Emergencies
(1) Fire is an ever-present hazard, especially where electrical equipment is concerned,
every staff is required to familiarize him or herself with the fire extinguisher
locations and the buildings emergency exits at his or her office premises.
(2) Fire extinguisher locations, the buildings emergency exits and fire assembly point
locations shall be pointed out to all staff during their orientation, every staff shall
know where the fire extinguishers are located and how to operate them effectively,
this information shall be reviewed periodically.
114. Occupational Safety
(1) The Authority shall be guided by the laws relating to occupational health and safety
as established by the competent authorities.
(2) The goal of the Authority in occupational health and safety is to proactively
take preventive measures to assure staff and other stakeholders of a safe and good
working environment, free of accidents, injuries or ill-health.
115. Infectious and Life-Threatening Diseases
(1) The Authority shall respond to staff with infectious and life-threatening illness
with support, compassion and understanding by giving the same consideration
as staff with any other illness.
(2) A staff who has a life-threatening illness shall continue working as long as he or
she may perform the essential functions of his or her job and possess no health risk
to others.
5 1

(3) Staff who has infectious disease like Meningitis, Ebola, Tuberculosis,
Conjunctivitis, Cholera and any other declared as infectious shall only be allowed
to return to work when a doctor certifies that he or she can return to work.
116. Insurance and Workman’s Compensation
The Authority shall endeavor to facilitate health insurance and workman’s compensation
insurance for its staff with relevant agencies.
CHAPTER X
COMPLAINT AND GRIEVANCE PROCEDURES
117. Staffs Rights and Responsibilities
(1) The Authority shall avail, sensitize and create awareness on staffs’ rights,
responsibilities and Authority’s policies, regulations and procedures.
(2) It is the responsibility of each staff to learn, understand and consistently observe
the rules, procedures and standards of conduct established by the Authority.
(3) All staff are eligible to access the provisions of the grievance procedures.
(4) Filing of a grievance shall not jeopardize the staff’s position, opportunities for
advancement or salary increases.
(5) Staff may not be forced by management or any other staff into not proceeding
with a grievance or not appearing as a witness at an inquiry.
(6) All staff, (including the grievant) shall cooperate at all stages in an
investigation of a grievance or misconduct, this cooperation shall include, but not
be limited to, appearing to answer questions and presenting truthful information,
failure to present truthful information may result in disciplinary action.
(7) If any party involved is dissatisfied with the outcome of any stage in a disciplinary
or grievance inquiry, movement of the inquiry to the next stage may be requested.
(8) The Authority recognizes the meaningful value and importance of full discussion
in resolving misunderstandings and preserving good relations between
management and staff.
(9) Shall a condition exist that a staff feels unsatisfactory, he or she shall bring it to
the attention of the appropriate person in the proper manner.
(10) The Authority is to provide conducive working environment where staff realize
their full potential.
5 2

(11) The Authority shall ensure that staff’s performance is not hampered due to
unresolved differences.
(13) The Authority shall provide aggrieved staff with a mechanism through which their
grievances are addressed.
118. Resolving Complaints and Grievances
(1) Staff are required to bring complaints to the attention of their immediate
supervisor in the first instance, the supervisor is required to respond to the
complaint within five (5) working days. A resolution is encouraged at this stage
through discussion and counselling.
(2) If the staff and supervisor’s discussion does not settle the matter, the staff next
step of action is to submit to the supervisor a written grievance and the following
need to be adhered to:
(a) the supervisor is required to respond in writing within three (3) working days.
Copies of this communication shall be sent to the Commissioner for Corporate
Service;
(b) a resolution is encouraged at this stage through discussion and the
counselling of all parties concerned. In case the grievance is not resolved or
where the supervisor is the offender, the matter may be referred to the next
management level;
(c) at this stage, the officer appealed to shall convene a meeting to review the
grievance and the complainant’s supervisor’s response, his or her hearing shall
be conducted in privacy with no interruptions;
(d) the complainant may choose to be accompanied by a colleague or any other
person who shall be staff, minutes of the grievance meeting shall be recorded
and be held in confidence.
(3) Both the Respondent and the Aggrieved party shall provide evidence and the
allegations be clearly stated, there should be adequate time for enquiry and cross-
examinations to and by both parties.
(4) If the grievance is not resolved at this stage, the supervisor handling the matter shall
have to forward it to the respective disciplinary committee.
(5) Having received the grievance, the disciplinary committee shall hear the
complaint and make recommendations in writing within seven (7) working days to
the Commissioner General for decision or further action.
(6) If the staff is still not satisfied with the recommendations by the disciplinary
committee and decision by the Commissioner General, he or she may further appeal
to the Board in writing, clearly stating reasons for his or her dissatisfaction, the Board
shall expeditiously determine the case and bring the matter to a conclusion.
CHAPTER XI
5 3

PERSONAL RECORDS, PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT
119. Personal Records
The Authority shall protect and safeguard the privacy of staff’s personal information
to the fullest extent possible, consistent with service and legal practices.
120. Registry Records
(1) The Authority shall collect, maintain and use staff personal information in such a
manner as to ascertain its accuracy and relevancy, preserve the confidentiality of
the information, serve business needs, and to ensure that they conform to applicable
legal requirements.
(2) To preserve privacy of the records, only those who have a legitimate “need to
know” may have access to staff information, the disclosure of such data is
governed by these Regulations.
(3) Personal files shall be reviewed to ensure that only pertinent and necessary data is
kept, the files for each staff shall be retained in accordance with the established
records retention policy.
(4) The personal files shall contain only documents that pertain to and are officially
used to record qualifications for employment, promotion, benefits compensation,
termination or disciplinary action such as:
(a) employment applications and personal history forms;
(b) curriculum vitae or resumes;
(c) copies of certificates, both academic and professional;
(d) copy of identity card, Authority card, driving license and passport;
(e) letters of employment, acceptance letters and testimonials or referees;
(f) salary information;
(g) documentation of compensation changes, employment, job titles, seniority,
birth date, authorization for pay deductions;
(h) termination or separation information;
(i) attendance records;
(j) fringe benefits information;
(k) retirement records;
(l) performance appraisal or evaluations;
(m) education information from colleges, technical schools and universities;
(n) leave applications and approvals records;
(o) promotion records;
(p) disciplinary records;
(5) All personnel data shall be electronically stored.
121. Personal Files
5 4

(1) The Department responsible for Human Resources shall maintain
both open and confidential files for each staff under safe environment.
(2) The Departments and State Revenue offices shall also maintain separate files for
each staff where records such as leave forms and personal data shall be kept.
(3) The Departmental or State Revenue office open personal file shall accompany the
staff in the event of a transfer to a different Department or State Revenue office
within the Authority.
(4) When staff leaves the Authority, the personal files shall be removed from active
files six (6) months after cessation of employment and be held for a period of
ten (10) years before it is destroyed.
(5) All confidential files for Board Appointees shall be kept under lock and key in
the office of the Commissioner General.
(6) Staff shall not handle his or her personal file, in case of any issue regarding a
personal file, the concerned staff shall contact the head of Department responsible
for Human Resources for assistance.
(7) In the case of files dealing with potential or actual litigation claims, access to
personal file by a staff shall be given to the staff in the presence of the legal officer,
the staff shall be permitted to make notes concerning any such information.
(8) Medical records shall be kept in staff personal confidential file, the records
shall be retained for the duration of employment plus ten (10) years, this includes
records of occupational injury and all types of treatment and testing by the
Authority.
(9) Medical records to which staff may be given access include reports of physical
examinations and laboratory tests made by physicians acting for the Authority, the
staff may also review physician’s statements concerning leaves of absence or work
restrictions.
122. Reporting Changes in Personal Records
(1) Each staff is required to report any change of his or her records kept in his or her
personal file such as name, address, telephone number, marital status and number
of dependents as well as any academic or professional qualification acquired such
as degrees or certificates to their supervisor and the Human Resource Department
within thirty (30) days of such a change.
(2) The Authority is not responsible for non-receipt of any official communication sent
to the staff, if the staff has failed to file a change of address notice with the head
of Department responsible for Human Resources.
5 5

(3) In case staff need to change the number of dependants, it is necessary for the
employee to notify the Commissioner for Corporate Service in writing as soon as
possible, attaching the necessary documents to support the change and to receive
acknowledgment from the same office.
123. Performance Management
(1) Performance management is an integral part of the human resource management
system and ensures that Authority deliver on its objectives.
(2) Performance management is a process by which an organization assesses whether
it is delivering the right services to the right people, at the right time and cost in
accordance with its mission and objectives.
(3) Authority is committed to achieving its objectives in performance by
ensuring a performance management system is in place to yield better results from
teams and individual staff members. This entail setting mutually agreed targets
between the supervisor and the staff, based on jointly agreed goals, standards and
competencies or skills requirements.
(4) Supervisors and managers are responsible for managing the performance of the
staff.
(5) At the beginning of every financial year, the Board shall give the direction to the
Management to provide for the corporate objectives that shall be achieved at the
end of the year. The direction shall be cascaded down to the heads of departments,
section heads and finally to the individual staff.
(6) Using performance management system, the Authority shall ensure that:
(a) the work performed by staff accomplishes the objectives of the Authority;
(b) staff have a clear understanding of the quality and quantity of work output
expected from them;
(c) staff receive on-going information about how effectively they are performing
relative to expectation;
(d) a wards and salary increase based on staff performance are provided
accordingly;
(e) opportunities for staff development are identified; and
(f) employee performance that does not meet expectations is addressed.
(6) The Authority shall ensure that the staff performance management process is an
important way to improve the effectiveness of the Authority through the best
performing staff.
124. Annual Performance Appraisal
5 6

(1) Staff performance appraisal shall be carried out the whole year round with
emphasis on feedback as the backbone of performance improvement.
(2) A formal staff performance appraisal is carried out annually. The appraisal shall
be documented on a standard form defined by the Authority, the annual
performance appraisal shall be used to report overall staff performance.
(3) Prior to discussing a completed performance appraisal i.e. an appraisal
containing ratings and descriptions of actual performance, with staff, shall avail
him or herself before an appraisal meeting where comparison of his or her ratings
with that of the supervisor shall be made.
125. Performance During Probation period
(1) The performance of new staff shall be reviewed either after three (3) months or six
(6) months depending on the job category, the purpose of this review shall be to
determine whether the staff has been able to perform his or her duties satisfactorily
and whether he or she shall be confirmed to employment.
(2) The respective commissioners or supervisors shall carry out a performance
evaluation to determine suitability for confirmation for permanent employment or
termination as the case may be, such evaluation shall be carried out and
communicated to the Division responsible for Human Resources at least one month
before expiry of the probation period.
(3) The probationary period may be extended for a period not exceeding one month
if management deems it necessary, where the staff probationary period is extended
the staff shall be informed in writing the reasons thereof.
(4) In case of an interruption during the course of probation, the probation may be
extended to cover the period of absence.
(5) If the staff has not performed to the expectations of the Authority, but there is a
reason to believe the staff may be able to do so if allowed, additional probation
period may be extended, counselling shall be done and staff counselling record be
maintained.
(6) The staff shall be notified of the decision by the last day of the probationary
period. If he or she is absent, the probationary period may automatically be
extended until the close of business on the first day the staff returns to work.
(7) The appointing authority or a newly recruited staff on probation may terminate
appointment at any point before the probationary period expires by giving a twenty-
four (24) hours’ notice.
5 7

126. Poor Performance
(1) Where the staff performance falls below expectations at any time during the
performance cycle, the supervisor shall document the performance deficiency and
take actions, including (if appropriate) disciplinary action, to assure that
performance expectations shall be met within a reasonable period of time.
(2) The supervisor shall document the performance that falls short of expectations
by preparing a corrective action plan or other documentation. The document shall
specify:
(a) the performance problem;
(b) the steps to be taken to improve performance, including timeframe for
improvement;
(c) the consequences of failure to improve; and
(d) a follow-up meeting date.
(3) A corrective action plan shall be considered successfully completed only when
the staff actual performance has improved to the point where expectations are
being met.
(4) The methods by which staff shall be appraised and the job descriptions to be used
as indicative of performance shall be determined from time to time and approved
by the Board.
(5) There shall be staff performance appraisal report, which shall be completed
annually in writing in respect of every staff by his or her supervisor based on
continuous appraisal and discussion during the year.
(6) When assessing staff performance, the supervisor shall take into account:
(a) professional or academic qualifications and experience;
(b) knowledge of work;
(c) output and speed of work;
(d) tact, courtesy and grooming;
(e) ability to co-operate with colleagues and persons placed in authority over him
or her;
(f) personal conduct;
(g) other special merit or outstanding achievements during the year under review;
(h) integrity.
(7) Every appraiser shall ensure that the appraisal report is completed accurately,
without any bias or prejudice and to the best of his or her knowledge.
(8) Every appraise shall be given the opportunity to see and discuss their appraisal
form with the appraiser before signing it.
5 8

(9) The performance appraisal report shall be countersigned by the appraiser’s
supervisor or reviewer who shall be at liberty to discuss the appraisal report with
both the appraiser and appraise.
127. Appraisal period
(1) The appraisal period shall be one year except during the probation period.
(2) The annual performance appraisal report shall be a summation of the staff annual
performance.
128. Performance Appraisal appeal
(1) Any staff not satisfied with the supervisor’s appraisal may refer the matter to the
respective Head of Division and Department who shall arbitrate and find a solution.
(2) If the matter is not resolved, it may be brought to the attention of Commissioner
for Corporate Service, the matter shall be disposed of fairly within one month.
129. Continuous Performance Appraisal
Performance appraisal shall be an on-going continuous exercise throughout the
performance period, milestones over the review period shall be documented and
maintained in the appraiser’s personal file.
130. End of Year Appraisal
(1) The open-ended performance appraisal system shall be used to review the
performance of staff on the basis of performance objectives which have been set
and agreed upon in advance.
(2) Every staff shall be responsible for completing the performance appraisal form
annually rating him or herself objectively and discussing his or her own
performance objectives and development plans with his or her supervisor
(3) The End Year Appraisal shall take place at the end of the appraisal period. The
appraiser and appraise shall meet at the end of the year to discuss the overall
performance over the appraisal period.
(4) Prior to the meeting, the appraise shall prepare a preliminary assessment of the
extent to which his or her set performance targets have been achieved as agreed at
the beginning of the performance period.
(5) The appraiser and appraise shall discuss the agreed performance targets together
with any changes or comments from the mid-year performance appraisal.
5 9

(6) The appraiser shall assess the extent to which the appraise has achieved the
performance targets set, taking into account any unforeseen developments that may
have affected performance during the period, the appraiser shall also assess the
appraiser’s core competencies and values and indicate his or her views in the
appraisal form.
(7) The supervisor shall be responsible for rating the performance of the staff
against set objectives and discussing with the staff the performance objectives for
the following review period.
(8) The completed form by the supervisor shall be submitted to the respective Head
of Division or Department, the Head of Division and Department shall be
required to assess whether the appraisal has been conducted in a fair and objective
manner and whether the set objectives are realistic and in line with the overall
objectives of the Division, Department and the Authority
(9) The Commissioner for Corporate Service shall cause the appraisal forms to be
filed in the personal confidential file of the staff and a copy of the appraisal form
shall be provided to the staff.
131. Recognition and Commendation
The process of performance appraisal shall assist the management to make decisions in
the following areas:
(a) Reward and sanction in relation to performance.
(b) Identification of job-related staff development needs or training needs.
(c) Confirmation in appointment.
132. Adverse Appraisal Reports
(1) Staff who receives an adverse performance appraisal report shall be liable to a
written warning, for the purpose of these Regulations adverse performance means
staff performance rating below 50%.
(2) If there is no improvement in work performance in the following appraisal period
the staff shall be liable to further disciplinary measures including demotion.
(3) Any grievances arising from the use of the appraisal system shall be resolved in
accordance with the approved Authority grievance procedure.
CHAPTER XII
COMPENSATION, SALARY AND ALLOWANCES
133. Compensation
(1) The Authority recognizes and is committed to the sound management of its staff total
compensation as an essential component in the effective management of personnel
6 0

in the authority, this is to ensure cost-effectiveness, efficient and effective
formulation and implementation of Authority policies and programmes,
(2) Compensation consists of both salary and non-salary elements. Salary elements
include basic salary and performance awards, non-salary elements include benefits
such as retirement on medical grounds, disability allowance, pension, job specific
allowances and death-related benefits.
134. Remuneration
The Authority shall endeavour to have a fair competitive and attractive remuneration
scheme so as to be able to recruit, motivate and retain qualified staff.
135. Entry Points
(1) A newly appointed staff shall be placed at the appropriate salary scale approved
for such a grade.
(2) There shall be a file for every staff maintained at the Corporate Service Division,
the Corporate Services Division shall provide the personal numbers after
identification of the staff.
(3) Salaries shall be paid as per the letter of appointment indicating acceptance of offer
with effect from the date the staff reported for duty.
(4) Removal of staff from the payroll shall be directed by the Commissioner for
Corporate Service and may be on account of resignation, death, retirement,
dismissal, and termination of contract or expiry of contract.
(5) All salaries shall be paid through the staff bank accounts except for casual staff
who shall be paid on a daily basis and may need to identify themselves using their
national or other appropriate identification cards when receiving their cash
payments.
(6) A casual staff who may be engaged for more than a day may elect to be paid the
accumulated wages through a bank account.
(7) The Department responsible for human resources shall be responsible for ensuring
timely preparation and payment of salaries and wages to staff.
(8) The Head of Department for Human Resources shall ensure timely prepared payroll
th
is submitted to the Commissioner for Corporate Service by 15 day of every month
for verification and confirmation before the Commissioner General’s approval for
the Finance Department to execute the payment.
6 1

(9) In collaboration with the Finance Department, the Human Resources and
Administration Department shall ensure that statutory and other deductions are
affected and remitted to the relevant authorities.
(10) The Human Resources Department and the Finance Department shall ensure that
only bona fide staff are paid salaries.
136. Salary Administration
(1) The determination of salaries and salary scale shall be in accordance with the
organization structure, Scheme of Service and salary structure, the salary paid
to staff is initially dependent on the entry grade and subsequent increments shall
be based on the individual’s performance.
(2) Any grievance with respect to the job grade or salary shall be lodged through
the Head of Division or Department who shall forward it to the Commissioner for
Corporate Service.
137. Payroll
(1) Staff names shall be added to or deleted from the Authority payroll only upon
written instructions from the Commissioner for Corporate Service.
(2) Staff salary shall only be changed through a written authorization from the
Commissioner for Corporate Service.
138. Payment of Salary
(1) It is a policy of the Authority to pay salaries promptly after the necessary statutory
deductions have been made, an individual staff remuneration package is
confidential and shall not be discussed with other staff.
(2) The pay period for all permanent and contractual staff shall be on a monthly
basis, with salaries being processed not later than the last day of the month. Net
payments shall be sent directly to the bank accounts of staffs.
(3) Salary shall not be paid in cash.
(4) The Commissioner for Corporate Service shall ensure only bona fide staff are
captured in the payroll system on time and paid their salaries as provided in their
letters of appointment or contract and annual increments.
(5) Salary slip indicating basic salary, gross salary, deductions made, resultant
net salary and outstanding Authority liabilities shall be forwarded to staff every
month. The head of department responsible for finance shall forward a copy of
monthly paid payroll to the Commissioner for Corporate Service, for
reconciliation.
6 2

139. Payroll Deductions
(1) Staff monthly salary shall be subject to statutory deductions and other deductions
as may be agreed or instructed by the staff.
(2) The Authority shall withhold statutory deductions and relevant taxes from each
staff gross salary. In addition, deductions shall be made from staff salary for
benefits such as retirement contributions, advances and other monies owed to the
Authority as well as any other amount specified by the staff such as insurance.
(3) Staff shall complete the necessary forms and inform the human resources
Department in writing of those deductions they authorize at the beginning of their
employment or when they occur. All changes to the payroll shall be effected in
writing through a Pay Change Advice (PCA).
140. Annual salary Increments
(1) Every staff may be eligible for an annual salary increment until the maximum of
his or her salary grade, staff shall not be allowed to cross the bar into a higher salary
grade except on promotion or appointment to a higher post.
(2) Staff whose performance is unsatisfactory or below the required standard, shall not
be granted any increment or be allowed to cross the efficiency bar where
applicable, until they improve their performance.
(3) Annual increment is an award for good outstanding performance during a
particular period through the Authority’s discretion.
(4) The salary increment of staff may be withheld if:
(a) the appointing authority is satisfied that the staff has performed
unsatisfactorily;
(b) disciplinary or criminal proceedings have been instituted against the staff;
(c) the staff has been issued with a stoppage of increment for a breach of
the disciplinary code or unsatisfactory performance during the review period.
(5) Where it is decided that the s a l a r y increment(s) be withheld, the staff shall
be informed in writing specifying the reasons upon which the decision has been
based and when restored, no arrears shall be claimable.
141. Salary Review
Management shall review salaries from time to time to factor in the market trend subject
to the recommendation of the Board and the approval of the Minister.
6 3

142. Grading structure
The Board shall establish and maintain a staff grading structure based on job
requirements, qualifications and merit, the grading structure shall be reviewed regularly to
keep pace with the Labour market developments.
143. Salary Advances
(1) A salary advance shall be granted to staff owing to unforeseen circumstances,
which places him or her in a difficult financial position requiring assistance from
the Authority.
(2) To qualify for a salary advance:
(a) staff shall not have any outstanding salary advance or disciplinary case;
(b) recovery of the advance to be in three (3) months.
(3) In approving the salary advance, the approving officer is to ensure that it complies
with the one third (1/3) rule where the respective staff’s total deductions do not
exceed two third (2/3) of his or her basic salary.
144. Staff Benefits
A benefit is any gain that accrues to the staff by virtue of his or her employment or grade,
the benefits that exist at Authority are:
(a) medical benefit scheme;
(b) allowances such as house allowance, commuter allowance, leave allowance
and telephone allowance (where it applies);
(c) specific benefits are stipulated in individual staff letters of appointments or
contracts.
145. Pension or Gratuity Benefit Scheme
(1) Staff on permanent terms of employment shall be eligible for membership to
the Pension Scheme.
(2) Staff on permanent terms of employment shall be entitled to Authority
contribution to Pension Schemes.
146. Gratuity
Staff appointed on contract terms for a period of one (1) year and above, shall be eligible
for gratuity as stipulated in their letters of appointment and as per the existing law.
147. Allowances
6 4

The Authority shall pay allowances within the budgeted provisions, these allowances may
include house or rent, commuter, fuel, responsibility, entertainment, acting, special duty,
passage and baggage, leave, domestic worker, professional, electricity and water, security,
telephone, hardship, risk, furniture, clothing, car, motorbike loans, extraneous allowances
and any other that the Board may approve from time to time.
148. Commuter Allowance
Staff shall be entitled to commuter allowance. The rates of commuter allowance shall
be determined by the management and approved by the Board.
151. Hardship Allowance
Staff working in hardship areas as defined by the Authority shall qualify for payment of
hardship allowance. The rate of hardship allowance payable shall be as provided by the
Authority from time to time or by a negotiated Collective Bargain Agreement
152. Incentive Allowance
(1) This is an allowance paid to staff to compensate them for extra duties occasioned by
the demands of their busy offices.
(2) This allowance shall be paid to compensate such staff for the extra hours incurred
or working over public holidays and weekend as may be determined by the
management.
153. Subsistence Allowance within the Country
(1) When an officer travelling on duty is required to stay overnight away from his or
her permanent station and makes his or her own arrangements for boarding and
lodging, accommodation allowance shall be paid to him or her at the rates
determined by the management and approved by the Board.
(2) Eligibility for this allowance and the period of absence from the permanent
station shall be determined in each case by the Management taking into account
such factors as the distance, mode of travel, nature of assignment and the time taken
to travel from the permanent station to a specified destination.
154. Subsistence Allowance outside South Sudan
(1) Staff who is required to travel on duty outside South Sudan shall be granted
subsistence allowance at the daily rates as per the government rates as specified
from time to time.
(2) When staff travelling, boarding and lodging expenses are paid in full directly to the
hosting institution or hotel by the Authority or any other organization, a residual or
6 5

topping-up allowance of up to one-third (1/3) of the standard rate of subsistence
allowance may be paid to him or her to cover incidental expenses.
(3) An officer travelling on duty abroad is normally expected to regularize his or her
expenses within the standard rate of subsistence allowance.
(4) In very exceptional circumstances, for example, when hotels are heavily booked
during an international meeting and the staff has no choice of accommodation or
when the standard rate of subsistence allowance is insufficient for any other
justifiable reasons, consideration shall be given by the management for a refund of
the additional expenses on production of receipted bills in respect of actual
expenditure incurred.
155. Specified Individual Rates
The specified individual rate in respect of subsistence allowance payable to every
category of staff shall be determined by Management as per negotiated Collective Bargain
Agreement or any other existing regulations.
156. Telephone Allowance
Due to the nature of their duties and level of responsibility, some categories of staff may
be eligible for telephone allowance, the rates and eligible categories of staff for this
allowance shall be approved by the Board.
157. Transfer Allowance
(1) A staff who is transferred from one duty station to another shall be eligible to
transfer allowance in the following manner:
(a) the allowance shall be paid in addition to any other allowance for which the
staff is eligible;
(b) transfer allowance shall be paid once at the rate approved by the Board;
(c) the transfer shall be at least forty (40) kilometres away from the staff current
station.
(2) Transfer allowance shall not be payable if the transfer of such staff is temporary,
for instance, relief duties or for a period not exceeding three (3) months, such staff
shall be entitled to their subsistence allowance.
158. Acting Allowance
(1) Acting allowance shall be payable to staff who is called upon to perform duties
of a job position above his substantive post, following the temporary or permanent
vacation of the post by the substantive holder.
6 6

(2) The staff appointed to act shall in every way be qualified and experienced to perform
the duties of that particular post.
(3) The amount of acting allowance shall be calculated as the full difference between
the minimum salary applicable to the staff job and the minimum basic salary
attached to the higher post or 25% of the staff substantive salary, whichever is
higher.
(4) The qualifying period for the payment of acting allowance shall be a minimum of
thirty (30) days, continuous period, but the acting appointment should not continue
for a period exceeding six (6) months.
(5) The acting allowance shall also cease when the acting staff is confirmed to the
position or when the position is substantively filled
159. Expense Reporting
Where staff is paid any reimbursable allowance, they shall promptly and honestly
account for the same to the Authority within forty-eight (48) hours after completion of the
task or returning from a journey.
CHAPTER XIII
TERMINATION OF EMPLOYMENT
160. Factors Leading to Termination of Service
(1) Termination is cessation of employment.
(2) The services of the staff shall cease on:
(a) incapacity of the staff to perform work as required by the employment contract;
(b) repeated failure by a staff to perform work required to a satisfactory standard;
(c) disciplinary grounds or Gross misconduct of a staff at work or in the course of
carrying out his or her duties;
(d) changes in the operational requirements of the Authority of which the staff
has no capacity to operate;
(e) resignation;
(f) retirement;
(g) medical grounds;
(h) end of Contract;
(i) termination in lieu of reinstatement;
(j) removal in Public Interest;
(k) accepting appointment to another institution other than by way of secondment;
or
(l) death.
6 7

161. Notice of Termination
(1) An employment contract may be terminated by either the Authority or the staff:
(a) after continuous service by the staff for one year or more, one-month notice to
the other party;
(b) after continuous service by the staff for six months or more, but less than one
year, a two week notice of the other party;
(c) after continuous service by the staff for less than six months, one week notice to
the other party.
(2) The Authority shall not give notice to any staff who is on leave and, conversely,
staff shall not give notice to run concurrently with leave.
162. Termination for Incapacity
The Authority may terminate an employment contract where staff is incapable of
performing his or her work satisfactorily due to an illness or injury which is certified by
the Medical Commission to be permanent
163. Termination for Unsatisfactory Performance
The Authority may terminate staff whose performance is unsatisfactory and has been
repeatedly provided with a reasonable opportunity to improve but failed to improve, the
staff shall be notified of the possibility of termination and be provided with opportunity to
make a defense.
164. Termination on Gross Misconduct
(1) The authority may terminate staff for misconduct where there is evidence on
which the allegation is made and that the misconduct constitutes grounds gross
misconduct, the staff shall be given an opportunity to respond to the allegation.
(2) Staff shall be said to have been committed gross misconduct if he or she is found
to have:
(a) been rendered unable to perform his or her work effectively due to
consumption of alcoholic drinks, narcotics, psychotropic substances or additive
substances in workplace;
(b) been absent from work for a period of more than seventy-two (72) hours
without cause or satisfactory explanation;
(c) violated the fundamental rights of another staff, including, but not limited
to, having sexually harassed another staff;
(d) assaulted or altered any co-staff or a member of management at work place or
in circumstances which have a real and substantial connection to his or her
employment;
6 8

(e) negligently or intentionally destroyed or let property of the Authority to be
destroyed, resulting to losses to the Authority;
(f) negligently or intentionally exposed any of staff or other personal place of
work to risks in contravention of health and safety regulations;
(g) breached the Authority’s obligation to protect and keep secure confidential
information of Authority unless such breach has been obliged by law upon staff
or caused by the Authority or to protect public interest.
165. Termination Based on the Operational Requirements
(1) A staff may be terminated on account of redundancy due to changes in the
operational requirements of the Authority.
(2) If it is decided to restructure the Authority, a staff may be retrenched or laid-off,
declared redundant in consequence of restructuring for the purpose of facilitating
improvements in the Authority by which greater efficiency or economy may be
effective
166. Resignation
(1) Resignation is a voluntary decision by staff to terminate his or her employment with
the Authority.
(2) The resignation procedure shall be as follows:
(a) a staff who wishes to resign from employment with the Authority shall give
a written notice as per the terms and conditions of service;
(b) on the staff last day, the staff supervisor shall conduct an exit interview, after
the exit interview, the Authority property in the staff possession shall be
retrieved and information regarding final dues clarified;
(c) a staff on probation may resign by giving seven (7) days written notice. In this
case, the normal exit interview process shall also be undertaken;
(d) resignation of staff from the Authority shall be put in writing to the
Commissioner General, the resignation letter shall state reason for resignation
(optional) and the effective date of the resignation.
167. Retirement
(1) A staff of the Authority shall retire from service upon attainment of the mandatory
or voluntary retirement age as per Public Service Guidelines or negotiated
Collective Bargain Agreement.
(2) Six (6) months before retirement date of staff, the Human Resource Department
shall write and notify him of her impending retirement, the letter shall include all
information pertaining to the retirement including all the benefits due to the staff
at the time of retirement, the staff may write to the Authority to inform it about his
impending retirement, the processes to retire the staff can be effected from this
point.
6 9

(3) Where the Appointing Authority is of the opinion that reasons exist, for staff
serving on pensionable terms and who has attained the age of voluntary
retirement to be called upon to retire, the Authority may request the staff
concerned to show cause why he or she shall not be compulsorily retired.
(4) The Commissioner for Corporate Service shall forward any representations made by
the staff pursuant to notice given to him or her under sub-regulation (2) of this
regulation, together with his or her own recommendations to the respective
Appointing Authority, the appointing authority shall decide whether or not such
staff shall be called upon to retire, in the event staff accepts the Authority’s call
to retire, a special retirement package shall be paid as determined by the existing
applicable pension law.
(5) A staff wishing to retire voluntarily shall give notice of retirement six (6)
months in advance.
168. Determination of Age
(1) The date of birth shall be the date specified in the birth certificate or age
assessment and declared at the time of recruitment; provided that, where only
the year (and not the actual date) of birth of staff has been recorded, his or her
age shall be determined by deeming his or her date of birth to be the first day of
January of the year.
(2) Where only the month and year of birth have been recorded, the date of birth
shall be deemed to be the sixteenth day of that month (fifteenth in the case of
February).
169. Retirement on Medical Grounds
(1) Where the Authority is of the opinion that staff is incapable of satisfactorily
discharging the functions of his or her office due to ill health, or if the staff so
request, it shall call upon such staff to present him or herself before an approved
medical doctor with a view to ascertaining whether or not such staff is incapable.
(2) After the medical doctor has examined, the doctor’s report has to be certified by
the Medical Commission, the report of the examination with recommendations, by
the Commission shall be forwarded to the Commissioner General for a decision.
(3) A period of one-month notice shall be given to staff who is required to retire on
medical grounds.
170. Death of Staff
(1) The contract of employment of staff in Authority shall come to end one month from
the death of staff, unless it is otherwise legally determined.
7 0

(2) Upon death of staff, the Authority shall provide assistance to his or her immediate
family as per the terms and conditions of service and the CBA.
(3) In case of death of a staff, the terminal benefits shall be made to the deceased staff’s
next of kin.
(4) To avoid legal tussles, the Authority shall pay these benefits to the legally
recognized next of kin only as indicated by the deceased staff and recorded in the
personal file.
171. Terminal Benefits
(1) Staff whose employment is terminated by the Authority shall be eligible for all
applicable benefits.
(2) On termination of employment, staff shall be entitled to the following terminal
benefits, provided that any staff, who are convicted of any criminal offence
which involves corruption or embezzlement of the public funds, shall forfeit all
his or her rights or claims.
172. Clearance
A staff shall surrender all Authority properties including Identity and Authority Card
immediately he or she ceases to be a staff of the Authority. Clearance Form shall be
filled in respect of that staff and verified by relevant parties prior to processing of terminal
benefits. In case of death of an employee the clearance form shall be completed in
consultation with spouse or near relative of the deceased staff.
173. Certificate of Service
(1) The Authority shall give a certificate of service to staff who resigns or have to leave
the Authority, the certificate shall state the dates of commencement and termination
of employment, position held, reason for termination and any other relevant
information.
(2) A staff leaving the Authority shall receive a certificate of service from the
Commissioner for Corporate Service after they have been officially cleared.
174. Membership to Workers Unions
(1) The Authority Management recognizes any workers’ union that has successfully
concluded a collective bargaining agreement with the Authority.
(2) A staff is free to join their respective unions in order to articulate their grievances
and negotiate with the Authority on matters of mutual concern and regarding their
terms and conditions of service.
7 1

(3) Meetings of staff unions may not take place during office hours without
permission from the Commissioner General.
175. Transport
(1) When staff is travelling on duty outside his or her duty station, official transport
shall be availed.
(2) Where official transport is deemed as inconvenient and or uneconomical, use of
public transport shall be allowed, unless it is considered convenient for the staff to
use his or her personal car with the express written approval of the Commissioner
General or someone delegated by him or her to undertake this activity.
176. Travelling by Personal Car
(2) Where the official transport is not available and the use of public transport is
considered unsuitable when travelling on duty, a staff may seek permission from
the Commissioner General through his or her Head of Department, to use his or her
own car.
(3) Permission shall normally be granted where the use of one's car is economical and
in the interest of the Authority.
(4) Where possible, officers shall travel together in one motor vehicle.
177. Traveling by Air
(1) When travelling on duty to another country, a staff shall normally travel by air.
(2) For all those who hold diplomatic, special and official passport travelling to any
foreign country shall get clearance from ministry responsible for foreign
affairs.
(3) Air travel on duty within South Sudan shall require the prior approval by the
Commissioner General or any other delegated staff. Such approval may be given
only if other modes of transport are unavailable or air travel is economical or where
the saving of time is paramount.
(4) Air booking for staff shall be arranged with the airline approved by the
management.
178. Reimbursement of Taxi Fare
7 2

(1) When travelling on duty, staff shall be reimbursed the cost of taxi fares at prevailing
rates from his residence to the official destination, provided that public or official
transport is not available.
(2) Staff who makes use of his or her own car in the aforesaid circumstances may
claim normal duty motor vehicle allowance as per approved rates.
(3) Claims for motor vehicle allowance or for the reimbursement of taxi fares shall be
certified by the claimant to the effect that no official transport was available.
179. Baggage Allowance by Air on Duty
Staff travelling on duty by air shall not normally be granted any baggage allowance in
addition to the free allowance on his or her air ticket, unless an excess is required for
official purposes in which case reimbursement for the excess baggage will be considered.
180. Authority Vehicle Register
(1) A register of all the Authority vehicles shall be maintained. The register shall
include the following particulars:
(a) description of vehicle
(b) chassis number
(c) engine number
(d) registration number
(e) the date the vehicle is put into service
(f) department to which allotted
(g) the date of disposal of the vehicle
(h) vehicle Inspection Dates
(i) vehicle Insurance Dates
(2) The vehicle log books shall be maintained by the Transport Section to provide an
operating record up to the time of its disposal.
(3) Authority vehicles shall periodically be inspected. Any damage or defect noticed
during inspections shall be recorded and reported to the Transport officer for action.
181. Immobilization of the Authority Vehicles
7 3

(1) Wherever official vehicles are garaged and parked the vehicles must be
immobilized by removal of the switch key, where driving cabins are provided with
doors with locks, the doors of the vehicles shall be locked and the keys moved.
(2) The Authority vehicles shall be parked or garaged only at designated places.
182. Drivers
(1) All personnel required to drive official vehicles shall have a valid driving license.
(2) A driver shall not drive a type of vehicle for which he or she is not licensed.
(3) Staff authorizing the use of the Authority vehicle by a driver who does not possess
a valid license shall be held responsible for any pecuniary loss to the Authority that
may result.
(4) The cost of annual driving licenses of established official drivers shall be met from
Authority funds.
(5) In exceptional circumstances, and with the written authority of the Commissioner
General, an official vehicle shall be driven by an officer other than an approved
official driver.
(6) An officer who fails to produce such written authority, in addition to the driving
license, shall be subject to severe disciplinary action. This requirement shall not,
however, apply to a senior officer who is allocated a vehicle for personal use.
(7) Drivers of the Authority must at all times set high standards of road safety, desist
from smoking, unnecessary talking, well-groomed and wear safety belts at all
times. The driver shall ensure the Authority Vehicle assigned to him or her is in
good working condition and clean at all times.
183. The Transport Work Ticket
(1) The use of a work ticket for the Authority vehicle is mandatory. Any driver of the
Authority found operating without a work ticket properly authorizing the journey
in question, or found deviating from the route authorized, or found carrying
unauthorized passengers or goods, shall be subject to disciplinary action.
(2) The instructions set out in the front cover of the book of work tickets must be made
known to all drivers and other officers responsible for the management of the
Authority transport.
7 4

(3) A summary of fuel, oil, and distance travelled, shall be recorded, with the relative
work ticket number, in the vehicle log book on completion of each such ticket, or
at the end of each month shall a ticket remain incomplete at the end of that month.
A new work ticket shall be issued at the beginning of every month.
184. Maximum Speed
Drivers of vehicles of the Authority shall at all times observe the statutory speed limits
while not exceeding the maximum speed allotted to the class of vehicle being driven. The
maximum speed allowed shall be displayed on the dash board of the vehicle.
185. Use of Authority Vehicles
(1) The Authority vehicles are intended for official purposes and shall never be used
for private purposes such as business or pleasure.
(2) It is the responsibility of the relevant Head of Department to ensure that official
vehicles are properly and carefully used. An officer who makes improper use of
an official vehicle shall render himself liable to disciplinary action.
(3) In order to prevent unauthorized use of official vehicles, all officers are duty bound
to report to the appropriate authority and in detail any Authority vehicle which can
reasonably be suspected of being in unauthorized private use.
(4) Adequate comprehensive insurance cover of the vehicle, the driver and passenger’s
liability shall be taken at all times.
186. Ignition Keys
The ignition keys of all Authority vehicles, with the exception of ambulances, shall be
handed to the
Transport Officer or the officer-in-charge of the vehicle, outside office hours.
187. Government Vehicle Check Unit
The relevant police unit set up by South Sudan police is empowered to stop and check any
Authority vehicle and to prefer charges (where appropriate) against the drivers. Where the
charges are preferred on such checks, a report should be submitted by the driver to the
Transport officer.
188. Accident Reporting
(1) All officers and drivers in charge of vehicles of the Authority’s motor vehicles
shall acquaint themselves with provisions of the relevant traffic laws that make it
7 5

obligatory for a driver of a vehicle involved in an accident to stop and cooperate
with police officers and a response team.
(2) Under all circumstances, a driver involved in an accident shall report immediately
the facts of the accident to the nearest police station or police on duty.
(3) In addition to any report to the police, a detailed accident report shall be rendered
on the day of the accident to the transport officer, giving the following particulars;
(a) number of the vehicle and name of the driver;
(b) place, time and brief circumstances of the accident;
(c) name of any other person or persons, who have, or whose property has
suffered damage, or who have caused damage to the vehicle of the Authority
and the number of their vehicles;
(d) estimate of damage suffered by the Authority vehicle or its personnel or
property or both;
(e) the date on which the accident was reported and the name of the police officer
who took the report and the police station where it was made.
(4) Where the Authority incurs expenditure, whether by reason of any third party claim
or otherwise, as a result of any accident to any Authority vehicle and such accident
is wholly attributable or in part to the negligence or misconduct of any employee,
the latter may be required to reimburse to the Authority the whole or part of any
such expenditure.
CHAPTER XIV
MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
189. Anti-Harassment
(1) The Authority shall provide a work environment that is free from any form of
harassment, including sexual harassment and bullying, any form of harassment is
totally unacceptable and the Authority recognizes the adverse effect such behaviour
has both on people who work in the Authority as well as the clients.
(2) All staff and stakeholders, have a right to be treated with equality in regard to
dignity, concern and decency. Any action or inaction, communication or behaviour
that may reasonably be interpreted as harassment or bullying shall not be tolerated.
(3) The Authority provides impartial processes for dealing with harassment and
bullying and assists in the resolution of complaints.
(4) Harassment of any kind, if proven, constitutes unacceptable behaviour, the
Authority shall institute disciplinary action, if a staff is found to have been
engaged in harassment of any kind either against colleagues or other stakeholders.
7 6

190. Actions that Qualify as Harassment
Harassment may be in the form of racial, tribal, gender, marital status, religious or ethical
belief, disability, age, political opinion, employment status, family status, sexual
orientation, or involvement in carrying out the activities of the Authority, the following
also constitute harassment:
(a) The improper use of power based on administrative or managerial status to insult,
bully, dominate, manipulate, disadvantage or discriminate may also constitute
harassment.
(b) For the purpose of this sub-regulation, Bullying means repeated, deliberate and
targeted conduct by a person towards a member (or members) of the Authority
community which is offensive, intimidating or humiliating and which detrimentally
affects that member’s well-being.
(c) Romantic or sexual relationships between individuals in a supervisory, evaluation,
advising, coaching, or counselling relationship.
191. Reporting Harassment Cases
(1) A victim of any harassment shall act promptly report the matter to the respective
authority, such individuals shall seek initial guidance and advice from the head of
legal administration and any other relevant administrative officer within the
Authority, following such discussions, the person may choose: to take no further
action; to attempt to resolve the issue or to request formal intervention.
(2) If the aggrieved person undertakes to resolve the situation independently, the legal
officer shall follow up within reasonable time to ensure that the problem is
resolved.
192. Making a Formal Complaint
(1) Any formal complaint of harassment shall be made in writing to the Commissioner
General within seven days of the occurrence of the event.
(3) The person complaining (‘the complainant’) shall write a brief written summary of
the incident or incidents of alleged harassment, sign and date, the statement shall
be given to the person being complained about (‘the respondent’).
(3) Formal complaints shall be dealt with as quickly as possible, and in the normal
circumstances within one month. A decision shall be made by the legal officer
responsible in consultation with the parties, as to the most appropriate managed
intervention process in the circumstances.
(4) It is recognized that some alleged behaviour may constitute serious misconduct
and possibly a criminal offence to be referred to appropriate Disciplinary
Committee or external authorities.
7 7

(5) The legal officer may set up processes to resolve complaints impartially,
sometimes involving a mediator, such processes are confidential and agreed to by
both parties.
(6) Complainants have the right to withdraw the process at any stage, this does not
halt further investigation or action of disciplinary procedures.
(7) Regardless of the outcome of the proceedings, complainants shall not suffer any
consequences unless the accusations were deemed malicious.
193. Confidentiality
(1) The Authority shall maintain confidentiality on any cases unless there are
exceptional circumstances involving probable risk to the safety of any individual.
(2) Due to the possibility of defamation proceedings, all information shall be kept as
confidential as possible, complainants and respondents are advised not to discuss
any matters pertaining to a complaint with anyone other than those directly
involved or court.
(3) The Authority shall observe the principles of natural justice and procedural
fairness by ensuring that staff whose interests may be adversely affected by a
complaint is aware of the allegations against them, including the identity of the
person making the allegations, and given the opportunity to respond.
(4) The Authority may follow up on anonymous complaints where credible
information is provided.
(5) The parties involved with or affected by complaints dealt with under these
procedures are entitled to a fair hearing and are kept fully informed throughout the
process.
194. Sanctions that May Be Applied
(1) Allegations that are proved true shall be dealt with as per the disciplinary
procedures as set out in this Regulations.
(2) Alleged serious misconduct proved correct shall, with the consent of the
complainant, be referred to public prosecution attorney, this may include alleged
cases of physical assault, sexual assault and rape.
(3) Any person who made a complaint that is found to be false or annoying, sanctions
shall be applied through the normal disciplinary proceedings.
195. Representation
7 8

At any time during the proceedings of allegations on harassment, a complainant or
respondent may seek internal representation by any other staff for fairness and objectivity.
CHAPTER XV
GENERAL PROVISIONS
196. Visitors
Visitors to the Authority offices be guided as follows:
(a) Official visitors shall not be entertained without prior appointments.
(b) Visitors shall obtain visitors passes before proceeding to the respective offices.
(c) Receiving of official visitors into the offices shall be confined to Senior
Management and Head of State Revenue Offices only.
(d) Where necessary staff may meet with their visitors at the visitors or reception
lounges.
(e) Unofficial visitors shall not be allowed in the Authority offices at any time and day.
197. Communications
Only the Commissioner General or an officer authorized by him or her can make public
statements on behalf of the Authority.
198. Internal Communication
(1) Staff who wishes to submit matters for consideration by higher authorities shall
submit the same through his immediate supervisor or his or her Head of
Department. In forwarding letters sent through them the supervisor or Head of
Department or their representative shall give their appropriate versions or
comments.
(2) All correspondence shall be sent to the Commissioner General through the
respective Head of Division or Department provided that sensitive or confidential
information of ethical nature may be addressed directly to the Commissioner
General.
199. Use of Authority’s IT-Systems
Staff are responsible for using the Authority’s ICT resources entrusted to them in a
manner that is ethical, lawful and safe. The Authority reserves the right to access and
monitor the usage of these resources. Staff shall avoid abuse of the ICT resources
and shall comply with the Authority’s policies on information security and ensure that
information confidentiality, availability and integrity are not compromised.
200. Fund Raising
7 9

Permission shall be obtained from Management before fund raising or collections for
charitable activities are made in Authority premises.
201. Employee Property
The Authority will not be held responsible for the safekeeping of any personal property
of staffs left within the Authority premises.
202. Employer’s Right to Search
The Authority shall have the right to search any of its staffs within its office premises
where there is reliable evidence or reasonable ground that a staff has unauthorized item
in his possession, with the approval of the Head of Division/ Department, Head of State
Revenue office or Station in charge.
203. Loss, Theft or Damage of Authority Property
(1) Loss or damage of the Authority property including accidents involving
Authority property, burglary or theft of goods deposited in Customs, including
property entrusted to the Authority or in Bonded warehouses shall immediately
be reported to the immediate supervisor, Head of Division or Department or the
police as the case may be.
(2) Where the staff by his or her act, omission by his or her negligence, misconduct
or by reason of his or her failure to take reasonable care or to discharge his or her
duties in a reasonable manner, causes the Authority to suffer any loss or damage to
any property, the amount of such loss or the value of the property damaged or an
amount equal to the cost of repairing such property or such portion of such amount
or value as the appropriate authority may determine, may be recovered from such
staff.
204. Evidence by Staff
(1) Any staff called upon to give evidence, whether within or outside the
Authority, in any matter involving the Authority and which he or she is conversant
shall provide true and consistent evidence.
(2) Where staff is required to appear in court as a witness in a case which the
Authority is a party, that staff shall seek clearance from Commissioner General.
Upon such clearance being given, when appearing in court, such staff shall
endeavour to protect the interests of the Authority
8 0

205. Legal Proceeding in Court
The Board or the Commissioner General shall not be held liable for any act or omission
done bona fide or lawfully in the course of executing the powers, mandate and functions
of in event there is damage arising out of such act or omission. The Authority shall be
vicarious liable for such act or omission.
206. Legal Representation
(1) When a civil or criminal action is instituted against staff, Board member as a result
of their official position or an act done or committed in good faith when executing
official duties on behalf of the Authority, the Authority shall assist to engage an
advocate:
(a) if the staff loses the case and is required to pay any sum by way of damage,
costs, fine or compensation, such payment may be met by the Authority.
(b) If the staff is successful in his or her case and is awarded a cost and or damages,
he or she shall be required to refund the Authority the amount of financial help
he or she received or the amount of damages and or cost recovered, whichever
is less.
207. Savings and Credit Societies
Staff may be allowed to form and take part in credit and savings society at place of work
following Management approval.
208. Handing Over Report
(1) In re-deployment, transfer or termination of appointment, staff shall prepare a
comprehensive handing over report under the supervision of the immediate
supervisor.
(2) A copy of the handing over report dully approved by the supervisor shall be
submitted to the Human Resource section. In addition, the staff shall handover all
assets and equipment of the Authority that were at his or her disposal.
209. Amendment of the Regulations
These Regulations shall be amended within the framework of the Civil Service Act, Labour
Act and its Regulations or any affected related matter.
